question: Where is the definition of what a service provides, or does not provide, specified?
explanation: Service scope establishes a service’s boundaries, defining its included offerings and exclusions.

question: Which catalog-item type can be found in a Service Catalog?
explanation:
A record producer is a Service Catalog item type that provides an alternative way for users to create records, such as incidents, through the catalog. Requested items are generated by requests, categories organize catalog content, and execution plans define fulfillment.

**Learn more:** [Types of catalog items](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/r_ExtendedCatalogItemFunctions.html)

question: Which kind of catalog item can be found in a Service Catalog?
explanation: A Service Catalog can include content items, which provide informational or navigational content within the catalog. Requested items are generated request records, categories group catalog entries, and execution plans define fulfillment activities.

question: In the baseline Change - Normal model, how can Change Tasks be added? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Automatically via the Change - Implementation subflow

options.label: B
options.text: Manually by the user during New, Assess, and Authorized states

options.label: C
options.text: Automatically depending on the category selected on the Change Request

options.label: D
options.text: Manually by the user during all states, except Closed or Canceled

explanation:
The baseline Change - Normal implementation flow automatically invokes the Change - Implementation tasks subflow, which creates implementation and post-implementation tasks. Users can also manually add Change Tasks in any nonterminal change state; Closed and Canceled changes are excluded. The selected category does not automatically generate Change Tasks.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Exploring subflows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-subflows.html)

question: As of Quebec, Problem task records automatically move from one state to another when the required fields are completed. What are those states?

options.label: B
options.text: On Hold to Work in Progress

explanation: In the Quebec Problem Management state model, completing the required fields automatically advances a Problem task record from **New** to **Assess**.

question:
During the lifecycle of a Problem record, you can click the **Re-Analyze** button to move backward in the lifecycle.

When you click **Re-Analyze**, which state is set on the problem record?
explanation:
The Re-analyze action reopens a problem for further investigation and changes its state to **Root Cause Analysis**. [ServiceNow: Investigate root cause of a problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/investigate-root-cause.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Investigate root cause of a problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/investigate-root-cause.html)

question: Where can a change manager specify the fields that must be completed before a change request can transition from the **New** state to **Assess**?
explanation:
Model State Transition Conditions control whether a change request can proceed through a defined change-model state transition. They can require that specified field values are populated before the transition from New to Assess is allowed.

**Learn more:** [Create predefined transition condition types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-predefined-transition-condition-type.html)

question:
Your customer wants to add a field to the **Something is Broken** record producer form.

Which formatter would you use to add the field?
explanation:
The Default Variables Editor is the formatter specifically applicable to record producers. It displays the values of the questions (variables) defined for a record producer on records generated from that producer.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog variable editors](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/service-catalog-variable-editor.html)

question: What should be used to explore the full hierarchy and table definitions for Configuration Management Database Classes?
explanation:
CI Class Manager centrally displays the complete CMDB class hierarchy in a tree view and provides access to CI table definitions, fields, relationships, and associated metadata.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: View and edit class definitions and metadata](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_ViewTableDefinitions.html)

question: A Portfolio Manager is mainly concerned with the performance of which hierarchy?

options.label: B
options.text: Portfolio Owner, Service Owner, Catalog Manager

options.label: C
options.text: Service Catalog, Catalog item, Requested item

options.label: D
options.text: Requested Item, Catalog Task, Task SLA

explanation: A Portfolio Manager manages and assesses service performance across the Service Portfolio hierarchy, which consists of the Service Portfolio, its Services, and their Service Offerings.

question: Which operational role or user persona is accountable for the overall administrative capabilities of a portfolio?
explanation:
A Portfolio Manager is the operational role responsible for overall portfolio administration, including creating and maintaining portfolio records and related portfolio structures.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Community: Typical Service Portfolio Management users](https://www.servicenow.com/community/spm-forum/spm-itbm-roles-amp-capabilities-spreadsheet/td-p/2807816)

question: Which types of conflicts are automatically identified on a change request? (select 3)

options.label: D
options.text: Another change for the same CI, at the same time

explanation:
ServiceNow Change Management detects scheduling conflicts when a CI is already scheduled by another active change at the same time, when the CI falls in a blackout window, or when the change is outside an applicable maintenance window. Company holiday schedules and assignee shift schedules are not standard conflict types.

**Learn more:** [Conflict detection](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/c_ConflictDetection.html?contentId=BQKQBXTXm3WHQQdfui0ddA) · [Create blackout and maintenance schedules in Change Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/t_CreateBlkoutMaintSched.html)

question: Which of the following can be linked to a service in the service portfolio taxonomy?
explanation:
A service is associated with a leaf taxonomy node. Non-leaf nodes organize child nodes, whereas leaf nodes display and manage their associated services.

**Learn more:** [Create taxonomy nodes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-portfolio-management/create-or-mod-SPM2-taxonomy-nodes.html)

question: On the **Create New** change landing page in Service Operations Workspace, which class label appears for the Emergency change model?
explanation: In Service Operations Workspace, the Emergency change model is classified with the **Break/fix** label, reflecting its use for urgent corrective changes.

question: Which of the following options may a survey administrator configure for an individual survey? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: The ability for end users to decline survey assignments

explanation:
A survey can have trigger conditions that determine when it is sent and to whom. Its survey definition also includes an **Anonymize responses** setting, which stores responses without the submitting user name.

**Learn more:** [Configure a trigger condition for a survey](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/t_CreateATriggerCondition.html) · [Modify a survey definition](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/t_ModifySurveyDefinitions.html)

question: Problem and Problem Task records automatically transition from **New** to **Assess** when which fields are completed? (select 2)
explanation:
In the default ServiceNow Problem Management state model, the transition from New to Assess requires the State and Assigned to fields. The State field is managed by the state model, while Assigned to establishes the responsible problem analyst; Configuration item and short description are not the default shared prerequisites for this transition.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Problem Task form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-task-form.html) · [ServiceNow — Assess a problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/assess-a-problem.html?contentId=Ot4dqQedMlalKArTGcgBKw)

question: What components make up a Flow Action?
explanation: A Flow Action consists of inputs that provide data, action steps that perform the work, and outputs that return results.

question: Which of the following can users do while configuring stages in Flow Designer? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Display the stages to the requester

options.label: C
options.text: Import a copy of a pre-defined stage set

options.label: D
options.text: Define the stage set in a subflow

explanation:
Flow Designer supports importing a copy of a predefined stage set from the Stage Sets table; changes to that copy do not change the original. It also supports adding and configuring stages in subflows, as well as flows.

**Learn more:** [Configure and add stages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/add-stages.html) · [Flow and subflow stages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-designer-stages.html)

question: When using Inbound Email Actions, what occurs if an email is received with neither a watermark nor a reference number?

options.label: A
options.text: New incident created from the message

options.label: B
options.text: New interaction is created from the message

options.label: C
options.text: Email is rejected and auto-reply sent to sender

options.label: D
options.text: New case is created from the message

explanation:
By default, ServiceNow treats an inbound email with no identifiable watermark or reference number as a new message and attempts to create an incident from it.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Inbound email actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_InboundEmailActions.html)

question: When using Agent Assist in the Agent Workspace, which examples of possible solutions can be automatically searched for and displayed? (select 5)
explanation:
Agent Assist displays results from configured contextual-search sources, including Knowledge and related ITSM or CSM records such as Problems, Changes, and Cases. SQL queries and Runbook Actions are not supported Agent Assist search-result source types. The standard ITSM set also includes Incidents, which is required to make five but is not present in the supplied choices. [ServiceNow Agent Assist documentation](https://horizon.servicenow.com/workspace/components/sn-agent-assist-uib)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Horizon Design System — Agent assist](https://horizon.servicenow.com/workspace/components/sn-agent-assist-uib) · [ServiceNow Community — What is Agent Assist?](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-blog/what-is-agent-assist/ba-p/2294049)

question: Which workflow is described as requesting approval from a knowledge base manager before the article moves to the retired state? The workflow is canceled and the article stays published if any manager rejects the request.
explanation:
ServiceNow’s default **Knowledge - Approval Retire** workflow requests a knowledge base manager’s approval before retiring an article. If any manager rejects the request, the workflow is canceled and the article remains published.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Knowledge workflows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/r_KnowledgeWorkflows.html)

question: What do you use to determine who can access specific items in a service catalog?
explanation:
ServiceNow User Criteria records control access to Service Catalog items and categories. Applying a user criterion through the Available For or Not Available For related lists determines which users may access a particular item.

**Learn more:** [Apply user criteria to items and categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_AppUserCritItemsCat.html)

question: Which Change Task Types are available by default? (select 3)
explanation:
The default ServiceNow Change Task Type values include Planning, Implementation, Testing, and Review. Therefore, among the listed values, Planning, Testing, and Review are the available default types.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a change task in Service Operations Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/create-change-task-sow.html)

question: Which Release types are available on the baseline release record?

options.label: B
options.text: Major, Minor, Upgrade, Emergency, Maintenance, Patch

options.label: D
options.text: Alpha, Beta, Snapshot, Nightly, Milestone, Release Candidate

explanation:
The baseline release record supports the release types Major, Minor, Upgrade, Emergency, Maintenance, and Patch. ServiceNow distinguishes major, minor, and patch application versions as release-version categories; the other choices contain change types or unrelated lifecycle labels.

**Learn more:** [Managing application versions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/managing-application-versions.html)

question: Which role can configure and manage Incident Management properties?
explanation:
The `incident_manager` role is assigned incident-administration responsibilities, including managing Incident Management properties. ServiceNow’s current role documentation also identifies Incident Manager as managing incident properties, while its newer granular Incident Admin role is named `sn_incident_admin`, not `incident_admin`.

**Learn more:** [Components installed with ITSM Roles — Incident Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/inci-roles-instld-itsm-roles.html) · [Granular admin roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/granular-admin-roles.html)

question: The Major Incident Management (MIM) application is connected to the Incident Management process, but its records include an additional set of States. What are these MI States?

options.label: D
options.text: New, Work in progress, Escalated, Communicated

explanation:
Major Incident Management uses its own lifecycle state in addition to the incident’s normal state: Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, and Canceled (spelled “Cancelled” in the listed choice). A candidate begins as Proposed, becomes Accepted when promoted, is Rejected when declined, and becomes Canceled when demoted or canceled.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: View major incident information on the Incident form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/t~YvqQkg2oQX4L7ySrpyuQ/_CVlrJCKwN4J5NwQd~fHDA)

question: Which property on an order guide passes variables from one item to another item when the variables are equivalent?
explanation:
The **Cascade variables** property passes values from order-guide variables to corresponding variables on the ordered catalog items when the variables have matching names. [ServiceNow: Cascade an order guide variable](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_CascadeTheOrderGuideVariables.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Cascade an order guide variable](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_CascadeTheOrderGuideVariables.html)

question: Which catalog property lets users save partially completed requests so they can finish and submit them later?
explanation:
The **Enable Wish List** catalog property allows users to save catalog items, including entered information, and return later to complete the ordering process before submitting. [ServiceNow: Saving catalog items to a wish list](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-items-wishlist.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Saving catalog items to a wish list](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-items-wishlist.html)

question: Which user roles can communicate a workaround or a fix? (select 2)
explanation:
The **Communicate Workaround** and **Communicate Fix** actions are available to users with the `problem_admin` or `problem_coordinator` role (among other unlisted qualifying roles). A `problem_task_analyst` can work on problem tasks but is not authorized for these problem-level communication actions.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Communicate workaround for Problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-workaround.html) · [ServiceNow: Communicate a fix](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-a-fix.html)

question: Where can you enable the **Search as** feature for an incident?
explanation:
The **Enable search as** setting is in the **Search as** section of a Contextual Search table configuration record. The Incident [incident] related-search-results table configuration is therefore where this feature is enabled.

**Learn more:** [Configure table for a contextual search](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/platform-administration/contextual-search/t_DefineContextualSearchForForm.html) · [Enable viewing of search results for the current and another selected user](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/contextual-search/t_SearchAsDifferentUser.html)

question: After a Catalog Item has been requested, which mechanism determines the approvals and tasks that are triggered in the application?
explanation:
A ServiceNow Flow associated with a catalog item runs when that item is requested and orchestrates its fulfillment. The flow can request approvals and create catalog tasks through its configured actions.

**Learn more:** [Create a flow with a Service Catalog trigger](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-sc-flow.html) · [Create Catalog Task action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-catalog-task-flow-designer.html)

question:
A new problem manager needs a high-level view of activities in problem management.

Which module do you recommend?
explanation:
The Problem Management dashboard provides a high-level view across the full problem-management process, from opening through closing. [ServiceNow: Problem Management dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-management-dashboard.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Problem Management dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-management-dashboard.html)

question:
A customer wants Problem records to be automatically assigned to the Support group associated with the CI on the problem record.

Which existing business rule meets this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO

options.label: B
options.text: Populate Assignment Group based on Cl Support Group

options.label: C
options.text: Problem Assignment Group based on CI Support Group

explanation:
The out-of-box **Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO** business rule populates a Problem record’s Assignment group from the support group on the selected configuration item; it can also use the service offering where applicable. [ServiceNow: Legacy Problem form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-service-management/problem-management/legacy-problem-form.html?contentId=dQCL_mFcqHShO~vSWDXB0A)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Legacy Problem form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-service-management/problem-management/legacy-problem-form.html?contentId=dQCL_mFcqHShO~vSWDXB0A)

question: Which interface is intended for tier 1 IT agents who resolve internal or external customer issues?
explanation: IT Service Management Workspace (Agent Workspace) is the agent-focused ITSM interface for triaging, managing, and resolving customer issues such as incidents.

question: Where can a change manager specify the conditions that must be satisfied before a change request moves from one state to another?
explanation: Model State Transition Conditions configure the requirements that must be met for a change request to transition between states within a change model.

question: When editing a Change Flow, a library of reusable components is available for use in the flow. What are these components called?
explanation: ServiceNow Change Management provides reusable flow actions that can be added to Change Flows through Workflow Studio and the ITSM spoke.

question: Which functionality can be used to define the sequence of activities required to complete catalog items? (select 2)
explanation:
Service catalog workflows define the activities used to process a catalog item, and a Flow Designer flow associated with a Service Catalog item runs its configured actions to automate fulfillment. Both mechanisms can establish the ordered fulfillment process for a catalog item.

**Learn more:** [Service catalog workflows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogWorkflowDefinition.html) · [Create a flow with a Service Catalog trigger](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/task/create-sc-flow.html)

question: Which tools are available to an assignee to help resolve an incident? (select 2)
explanation:
Knowledge Articles provide documented troubleshooting and resolution information. Known Errors identify problems with known causes that do not yet have a permanent fix, often including a workaround; IT agents can use the Known Errors module to reduce investigation time for similar issues.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Data for problem resolution](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-service-management/problem-management/c_GatherProblemData.html?contentId=Arb1bWlwz4i~r4F0u0CMqw) · [ServiceNow: Problem Management process](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/c_ProblemManagementProcess.html)

question: What different methods can a user use to provide feedback on a knowledge article? (select 4)
explanation:
Knowledge article feedback includes adding or replying to comments, marking an article as helpful or not helpful, flagging incorrect or inappropriate content, and rating the article on a 1-to-5 star scale.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Provide feedback on knowledge articles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/r_KnowledgeFeedback.html)

question: Which record type should you use for a Computer request?
explanation: A Catalog Item represents a specific product or service that a user can request through the service catalog, such as a computer.

question: Which baseline Change Flow automatically creates a Change task for a Post Implementation Review?
explanation:
The baseline **Change - Emergency - Review** flow processes emergency changes in the Review state and automatically creates the Change task used for the post-implementation review. ServiceNow documents this flow as a default Change flow for an emergency change in the review state.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Change flows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/it-service-management/change-management/change-flows.html?contentId=jteQHxwhE9qRK9XP3biQbQ)

question: What is the relationship between Releases and Projects?

options.label: A
options.text: Project tasks and Release tasks are interchangeable

options.label: B
options.text: Projects can be part of one or more releases

options.label: C
options.text: Project features are components of a release

options.label: D
options.text: Projects need to be completed before releases can be defined

options.label: E
options.text: Projects are used to do root cause analysis for releases

explanation: In ServiceNow Release Management, projects can be associated with one or more releases; projects and release tasks are distinct work records.

question: Which event triggers the Change - Normal - Assess Flow?

options.label: A
options.text: A Change request using the Normal Change model is moved to the Assess state

options.label: B
options.text: A Change request using the Normal Change model is created

options.label: C
options.text: A Change request using the Normal Change model is Low Risk, and is moved to the Assess state

options.label: D
options.text: A Change request using the Normal Change model is Assigned to a group

explanation:
The default ServiceNow Change - Normal - Assess flow processes a normal change after it moves into the Assess state; risk level and assignment-group changes do not independently trigger this flow.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Change flows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/xanadu-it-service-management/page/product/change-management/concept/change-flows.html)

question: What would you use to create a New Hire Employee request that allows ordering a workstation and company mobile?
explanation: An Order Guide lets a requester order multiple related catalog items through a single guided request, such as a workstation and a company mobile for a new hire.

question:
A customer wants to add a new Catalog Item to the Service Catalog.

Which process would be used to ensure that the new item is authorized?
explanation: Change Management provides the formal assessment, approval, and authorization process for introducing a new service catalog item.

question: What defines the trigger conditions for a Notification record?

options.label: A
options.text: Define specific groups and users as recipients

options.label: C
options.text: Enable the Send to Event Creator

options.label: D
options.text: Modify the conditions on the when to send tab

explanation:
A notification’s **When to send** tab contains the trigger type and the record or event conditions that must be met for the notification to be sent. Recipient definitions belong on **Who will receive**, while mail scripts control notification content.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html)

question: When the **Assignment group** is blank on an incident record, what occurs when an agent who belongs to multiple user groups selects the **Assign to me** UI action?

options.label: A
options.text: An error is displayed indicating the agent must manually assign the incident

options.label: B
options.text: The agent is prompted to select the Assignment group

options.label: C
options.text: The Assignment group field automatically populates with the agent's primary group

options.label: D
options.text: The Assignment group field will not populate

explanation:
An agent who belongs to multiple groups must select the appropriate Assignment group before the incident can be self-assigned, because multiple eligible groups make an automatic group selection ambiguous.

**Learn more:** [Work on an incident record in Service Operations Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/work-on-incident-sow.html)

question: In which table are incidents stored?
explanation:
ServiceNow stores standard Incident Management records in the `incident` table. The ServiceNow Table API documentation uses `/api/now/table/incident` to retrieve, create, and delete Incident records.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Table API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/rest-apis/c_TableAPI.html)

question:
A customer asks that, when a Service Desk agent clicks the information icon for the Caller's name, the quick-view frame displays only these fields:

- User name
- Manager name
- Email Address
- Employee ID

How would you update the quick-view frame?

options.label: A
options.text: Update the sys_popup view for the user table

options.label: B
options.text: Update the sys_quick view for the caller table

options.label: C
options.text: Update the sys_popup view for the caller table

options.label: D
options.text: Update the sys_quick view for the user table

explanation:
The Caller reference points to a User [sys_user] record. Fields shown when the reference information icon is selected are controlled by the referenced table’s `sys_popup` form view, so the `sys_popup` view for the User table must contain only the required fields.

**Learn more:** [Reference field icon](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ReferenceIcon.html) · [Reference field type](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ReferenceField.html)

question:
When creating a problem from an incident, **impact**, **urgency**, and **priority** are automatically populated from the incident record. The problem management process owner wants the problem manager to assess the problem’s impact and urgency, so those incident values must not be copied.

Which module would you use to make this change?

options.label: A
options.text: System Policy > Rules > Priority Lookup Rules

explanation:
Problem Management properties include the `com.snc.problem.create_from_incident.attributes` setting, which specifies the incident attributes copied to a newly created problem. Its default list includes impact, urgency, and priority, and the setting is available under Problem > Administration > Problem Properties. Removing those fields lets the problem manager assess impact and urgency on the problem; priority is calculated from those values.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Problem management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ja-JP/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-mgmt-properties.html?contentId=6pu0GgB7DIU1khCH6YFuQg)

question:
A customer uses an external system to carry out changes. They want to capture those changes in their instance for reporting and CMDB maintenance purposes.

Which baseline Change Model supports this scenario?
explanation:
The Change Registration model is used to capture change requests that originate in, or are controlled through, an external system. It records those changes in the instance for visibility and reporting without applying the standard approval workflow.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Change models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-service-management/change-management/change-models.html?contentId=K7x6w_RI0H_f~2UUYuInfw) · [ServiceNow: Configure the Change Registration change model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/configure-change-registration-model-scm.html?contentId=gB_vGmk2troUllXbdN_i8A)

question: By default, a business rule automatically sets an Assignment group on a change request record. How is that group determined?

options.label: A
options.text: Change group on CI record, or if empty, the Change group on the Service offering

options.label: B
options.text: Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service

options.label: C
options.text: Support group on CI record, or the default assignment group for the user

options.label: D
options.text: Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service offering

explanation:
For a change request, the default assignment-group source fields are Change group on the configuration item (CI) and, if that field is empty, Change group on the service offering. ServiceNow documents that the default fields for change requests are change group, unlike incidents and problems, which default to support group.

**Learn more:** [Create a change request in Agent Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/BgFKZnPHldZ62gGtzQ71Mw/cZZFYNfdM7ypDoSb~J9Mag)

question: An implementation includes legacy change types with workflows as well as new change models. Which **Change Create New** option supports this scenario?
explanation:
ServiceNow Change Catalog supports a phased change-management implementation by providing a single creation entry point for both legacy type-based changes that invoke existing workflows and new model-based changes. This lets both processing approaches operate concurrently during migration.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ITSM documentation — Create a Change model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-a-change-model.html?contentId=sDV0MpBQ8JbbqmWaKxCh_w) · [ServiceNow ITSM Applications release notes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/store-release-notes/store-rn-itsm-service-ops-workspace-apps.html)

question:
Incidents can be created and managed in the workspace by using UI layouts tailored for different personas, processes, and interfaces. Examples include:

- Default
- Major incidents
- Self Service
- Mobile

What are these UI layouts called in the Now Platform?
explanation: Views are named form-layout configurations that present records differently for particular user roles, processes, or interfaces, such as Default, Major Incident, Self Service, and Mobile.

question: When working in the Email Client, how does an Email Template differ from a Quick Message?

options.label: A
options.text: Email Templates are like forms that can be sent to the caller for completion; Quick Messages are primarily used by the Chat Bot

options.label: B
options.text: Email Template is defined and automatically applied when the email form launches; Quick Messages are defined and then can be manually applied by the user

options.label: C
options.text: Email Templates are included with ITSM; Quick Messages are new with Machine Learning

options.label: D
options.text: Email templates are defined by users with admin role; Quick Messages are defined by users with quick_message_admin role

explanation:
An Email Client Template defines default email content and related field values and is automatically applied when its configured table, conditions, and execution order match. A Quick Message is predefined message-body content that a user manually selects and inserts while composing an email.

**Learn more:** [Create email client template](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateAnEmailClientTemplate.html) · [Composing emails with quick messages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/quick-message.html)

question: When defining catalog categories and subcategories, which good practices should be followed? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Align categories with CMDB classes where possible

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the number of top-level categories to 8-10

options.label: C
options.text: Remember that items can only be assigned to one category

options.label: D
options.text: Do not go to deep with subcategories: go only 1-2 levels deep

explanation:
A usable service-catalog taxonomy keeps the top level limited to about 8–10 categories and restricts subcategory nesting to 1–2 levels, so users can find services without excessive navigation. ServiceNow also supports assigning a catalog item to multiple categories, so a single-category restriction is not a valid practice.

**Learn more:** [Service catalog categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogCategories.html)

question: What is the relationship between Service Catalogs and Catalog Items? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: A catalog item can be associated with one or more service catalogs

options.label: B
options.text: Access to catalog items is determined by the service catalog's assigned user criteria

options.label: C
options.text: Service catalogs may contain multiple catalog items

options.label: D
options.text: A catalog item can only be associated with one service catalog

explanation:
A catalog item can be shared among several service catalogs, and each selected catalog shows that item in its Catalog Items related list. Service catalogs can therefore contain multiple catalog items.

**Learn more:** [Share catalog items across catalogs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_ShareCatalogItemsAcrossCatalogs.html) · [Catalog Item form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-item-form.html)

question:
A customer requires distinct catalogs for the following:

- **Human Resources** — employee-facing — for submitting requests to HR
- **Customer** — external-customer-facing — for ordering company products and services

When these catalogs are created, in which table is their definition stored?
explanation:
ServiceNow stores Service Catalog definitions in the Catalog table, `sc_catalog`. Multiple service catalogs can be defined for different groups, including human resources and customer-facing audiences.

**Learn more:** [Multiple service catalogs setup](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_MultipleServiceCatalogs.html) · [CatalogJS - Scoped](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/CatalogJSScopedAPI.html)

question: Which of the following cannot be defined or configured through a Catalog UI Policy?

options.label: B
options.text: Apply a requirement to all form views

options.label: C
options.text: Setting a catalog category to visible

explanation:
Catalog UI Policies apply to variables and variable sets on catalog item forms, and their actions support Mandatory, Read Only, and Visible states for those form elements. Catalog categories are configured separately and are not targets of Catalog UI Policy actions.

**Learn more:** [Service catalog UI policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogUIPolicy.html) · [Service catalog categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogCategories.html)

question: Which two examples of Change Management Key Performance Indicators are included with Performance Analytics but unavailable in ServiceNow reporting? *(select 2)*

options.label: B
options.text: Count of Completed Changes per Month, by Change Type

options.label: D
options.text: Count of Completed Changes per Month, by Category

explanation:
ServiceNow’s Change dashboard identifies **% Successful changes** and **% Unauthorized changes** as Performance Analytics indicators. Performance Analytics collects indicator scores over time, whereas counts of completed changes grouped by month and a record field are standard report-style aggregations. [Change dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Change dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change.html) · [ServiceNow Success score indicators](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/Mr7qUatbFXax1_h~z60rmA/qzJW8gtdLOcO8D~6XUKcfQ)

question:
The Problem Manager wants Problem Coordinators to be able to re-analyze a Completed Problem.

Which module can they use to make this change?
explanation:
The `problem.closed.role.reanalyze_from_completed` Problem Management property controls who may re-analyze a completed problem. This property is configured in **Problem > Administration > Problem Properties**.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Problem management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-mgmt-properties.html)

question: What would you use to create Incident records from emails sent by users or systems?
explanation: An Inbound Flow Action processes inbound email and can create Incident records based on messages received from users or external systems.

question:
A new Problem Coordinator inadvertently created several problem investigations that must be deleted.

Which role is required to delete a problem record?
explanation: The `problem_admin` role has the administrative Problem Management permissions required to delete problem records. A Problem Coordinator can create and coordinate problem investigations but does not receive deletion authority merely from that role.

question: Incident management provides limited functionality for which advanced reporting capability?
explanation:
Incident Management includes Complimentary Performance Analytics for Incident Management, a limited base-system version of Performance Analytics. Full Performance Analytics requires a subscription and provides the complete functionality.

**Learn more:** [Try out Complimentary Performance Analytics for Incident Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/performance-analytics/r_StUpPAInctMgmt.html) · [Reporting incidents](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/incident-monitor-track.html)

question: Your customer wants to use the Service Catalog to create task-based records for end-user inquiries. Which Service Catalog capability can be used to generate these records?
explanation: Record Producers provide a Service Catalog form that creates a record in a designated target table from an end-user submission, including task-based tables such as Incident.

question: If a change model has both **Write roles** and **Can write** defined, which users can modify the change model record? (select 2)

options.label: C
options.text: Users that have the Write role(s) OR that match the Can write user criteria

options.label: E
options.text: Users that have the Write role(s) AND match the Can write user criteria

explanation:
Write access for a change model requires a user to hold one of the configured Write roles and to match the Can Write user criteria. Users with the `admin` role can also modify the record because administrators bypass these record-level access restrictions. ServiceNow documents Write Roles as roles that edit the change model and Can Write as editable access to the model.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a Change model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-a-change-model.html)

question: How is granular read and write access defined for a particular change model?

options.label: A
options.text: Configuring ACL's on the chge_model table

options.label: B
options.text: Configuring ACL's on the Create New landing page

options.label: D
options.text: Setting Advanced Security to true and applying user criteria

explanation: Granular access to an individual change model is controlled by enabling Advanced Security and assigning user criteria that govern who can read or write that model.

question: A new problem manager needs to learn how to create reports to monitor problem-management activities. What should you recommend they do before they create new reports?

options.label: A
options.text: Submit a New Report Request via the service catalog

options.label: B
options.text: Take the Performance Analytics fundamentals course

options.label: C
options.text: Go to Reports > View/Run > All, then search for Problem reports

options.label: D
options.text: Submit a request for the sn_report_creator role

explanation:
Existing reports should be reviewed before new ones are created so that an appropriate Problem report can be reused or adapted rather than duplicated. ServiceNow documents that Reports > View/Run opens the Reports list, and the All tab displays all reports the user can access.

**Learn more:** [View the Reports list](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/pt-BR/now-intelligence/reporting/r_ViewTheReportsList.html)

question: Which role, requiring a user license, enables users to authorize requests?
explanation: The approver_user role only requires a base user license rather than a fulfiller or ITIL license, and it grants a user the ability to view and act on (approve or reject) approval records assigned to them without conferring any other elevated access to ITSM tables.

question: When a class is designated as a Principal Class, what impact does this have on the Configuration Item (CI) field in change, incident, and problem records?

options.label: A
options.text: It hides the CI field completely.

options.label: B
options.text: It allows selection of only CIs within the Principal Class.

options.label: C
options.text: It allows the selection of all CIs, regardless of class.

options.label: D
options.text: It locks the CI field to prevent edits.

explanation:
A Principal Class designation automatically filters the Configuration Item field on incident, change, and problem records, limiting selection to CIs that belong to principal classes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: About principal classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-sa-principal-class.html) · [ServiceNow: Key CMDB success advisor concepts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-sa-key-concepts.html)

question: Which of these elements are automatically incorporated into the update-set name for items published through Catalog Builder? (select 2)
explanation:
Catalog Builder automatically creates update sets using a default name format that includes the catalog item name and a date-and-time timestamp: `CB_<Template Name>_<Catalog Item Name>_<Date and Time Stamp>`.

**Learn more:** [Transfer catalog items using update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/transfer-catalog-items-using-update-sets.html)

question: On an incident record, where are the fields displayed in the caller lookup select box defined?

options.label: A
options.text: The Caller lookup field on the [user] table

options.label: B
options.text: The ref_ac_column attribute from the dictionary entry

options.label: C
options.text: The ref_contributions attribute on the caller lookup form

options.label: D
options.text: The form design of the caller lookup form

explanation:
Reference-field autocomplete columns are configured in the field’s dictionary attributes through `ref_ac_columns`; this attribute specifies the reference-table columns to display in the auto-completion list. The `ref_contributions` attribute controls icons next to a reference field, rather than the displayed lookup columns.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Auto-complete for reference fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_AutoCompleteForReferenceFields.html)

question: In Change Management, what does a Model State include? (select 2)
explanation:
A Model State defines an allowed lifecycle state in a change model. It has associated Model State Transitions that specify the permitted paths to other states, and those transitions can have Model State Transition Conditions that control when a transition is allowed or automatic.

**Learn more:** [Configure change model states](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/configure-change-model-states.html)

question: Which types of service can be managed within the scope of Service Portfolio Management? (select 2)
explanation:
Service Portfolio Management is used to create and manage business services and technical services, including their offerings and related portfolio information. A technical service typically underpins a business service.

**Learn more:** [Create a service in Service Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-it-service-management/page/product/service-builder/task/create-service.html) · [Service offerings in Service Portfolio Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-portfolio-management/SPM2-service-offerings.html)

question: In the CAB workbench, how can the CAB manager identify Change requests to add to a particular meeting agenda? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Change requests meeting different conditions, like Risk level or Type

options.label: B
options.text: Change requests planned within a certain date range

options.label: C
options.text: Use any of the options on the Agenda Criteria Tab

options.label: D
options.text: Change requests for a certain Change Flow Definition

explanation:
CAB agenda criteria can select change requests through additional filter conditions, including fields such as risk level or type. The criteria can also use a planned start-and-end date range to select the requests for the agenda. ServiceNow documents the condition builder for specifying which change requests are added and the option to use a planned date range.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a CAB definition](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/define-your-cab.html)

question: A problem record is the parent of which record?
explanation:
A Problem Task is a child work record created for a specific problem; its Source problem field identifies the problem record for which the task was created.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Problem Task form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-task-form.html) · [ServiceNow: Create a problem task](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/create-problem-task.html?contentId=kywJSvRfDMWke4NRLmc76g)

question: How can you define the content tracked and shown in every Incident record activity stream?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure the Activity stream client script

options.label: C
options.text: Configure the dictionary entry for the Activity stream

options.label: D
options.text: Configure the available fields from the Activity stream filter

explanation:
The Activity formatter’s **Configure available fields** option controls which fields are available in the activity filter and therefore which field changes can be displayed in Incident activity streams.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Activity formatter](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ActivityFormatter.html)

question: Which new architectural features were introduced in Change Management in the Quebec release?

options.label: B
options.text: Change Flows, Change Designer and Change Approval Matrix

options.label: C
options.text: Change Models, Change Flows and State Transition Models

options.label: D
options.text: Change PIR Assessments, Change Designer and Change Approval Policies

explanation:
The Quebec Change Management architecture added Change Models, Change Flows, and State Transition Models. Change Models provide flexible configuration for change requests and depend on State Transition Models, while Change Flows provide the supporting process automation.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Change Management plugins](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/platform-administration/list-of-plugins.html) · [ServiceNow legacy state model and transitions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/c_ChangeStateModel.html)

question: A change user reports that, with the new Preapproved tab, they must search through many options to locate the **Reboot Windows Server** change. Because they use this change several times each day, this is inconvenient. What should you recommend to make it easier for the change user?

options.label: D
options.text: Drag the change tile to the Navigation pane

explanation:
ServiceNow Change Management allows frequently used change models, including preapproved changes, to be pinned for quick, repeated access from the Pinned tab.

**Learn more:** [Breaking the Change Barrier](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-blog/breaking-the-change-barrier/ba-p/2294272)

question:
A tester submitted a bug report because the **Create Known Error Article** link never appears under **Related Links** at any point in the Problem lifecycle. The tester also observes that the instance has no Known Error knowledge base.

What could be causing this?

options.label: A
options.text: The Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin has not been activated

options.label: B
options.text: The customer did not pay the bill for Knowledge management

options.label: C
options.text: Tester is not impersonating Problem Coordinator

options.label: D
options.text: The sn_known_error_write role is required to see the Create Known Error article link

options.label: E
options.text: The requirement was not in the stories

explanation:
The Problem Management Best Practice — Madrid — Knowledge Integration plugin enables creation of known error articles from Problem records and creates the knowledge base for known error articles. When it is inactive, the related link and Known Error knowledge base are absent.

**Learn more:** [Activate Problem Management Best Practice — Madrid — Knowledge Integration](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/act-pm-best-prac-madrid-know-int.html) · [Create a known error article](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/create-known-error-from-problem.html)

question: Your customer uses the baseline Create Incident Catalog Item and wants to add a few additional input fields. How should you update the catalog item?
explanation: Catalog Item Designer is used to edit a catalog item and configure its input variables, including adding fields that collect additional requester information.

question: On a Change Approval Definition record, what does the **Wait for** condition specify?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the change approval is sent to an individual user or a group

options.label: B
options.text: The state the change must be in before the approval notifications can be sent

options.label: C
options.text: The number or percentage of users from the approval group that must approve the change

options.label: D
options.text: The fields that must be populated before the approval can be requested

explanation:
The **Wait for** setting determines the approval threshold for a group approval: it can require the first response, all responses, or a specified percentage of users to approve. ServiceNow describes it as determining the approval timing and the percentage of users required when that option is selected.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Create approval definitions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-approval-definitions.html)

question: At which level in the service portfolio taxonomy are service commitments associated?
explanation:
A service offering consists of service commitments that define its specific level of service, including availability, scope, and pricing.

**Learn more:** [Add a commitment to a service offering in Service Portfolio Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-portfolio-management/define-SPM2-service-commitments.html)

question: Released in Quebec, which tool lets you delegate the creation and maintenance of common, simple-use-case Catalog Items to business users?
explanation:
Catalog Builder provides a guided, restricted experience for business users to create and maintain catalog items, while catalog administrators retain responsibility for advanced capabilities. It is intended for common and simple use cases.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Catalog Builder overview](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-builder.html?contentId=UaN6RrIqW5MWSeptJA2uaQ)

question: A customer wants to use Incident Tasks on Incident records. For efficiency, they want all Incident Tasks to close automatically when their parent Incident is closed or canceled. How can this requirement be met? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: On Incident Properties, for Autoclose Incident Tasks, select Yes

options.label: C
options.text: On Incident Properties, for Close open Incident Tasks when Incident is closed or canceled, select Yes

explanation:
The `com.snc.incident.incident_task.closure` property closes open Incident Tasks when the related Incident is closed or canceled. It is available as the Incident Properties setting **Close open Incident Tasks when Incident is closed or canceled**, and it can also be enabled directly as a system property. When enabled, open tasks become Closed Incomplete when the Incident is closed and Closed Skipped when it is canceled.

**Learn more:** [Incident Management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/incident-management-properties.html) · [Synchronization between an incident and its incident tasks](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/inci-inci-task-state-sync.html)

question:
Your Problem Manager uses a structured problem management process that includes a final review of the implemented solution and of data concerning incident reduction. When a problem is resolved after a fix is implemented, they want the Post Fix Review task to be created automatically and assigned to the Problem assignee.

Which feature would you use to meet this requirement?
explanation:
Flow Designer can run from a Problem record update when its state becomes Resolved, create a related Post Fix Review task, and populate its assignment dynamically from the triggering Problem record’s assignee. Its Create Task action supports creating Task-table extension records and setting fields with dynamic values from the flow trigger. [Create Task action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-task-flow-designer.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create Task action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-task-flow-designer.html) · [ServiceNow: Flow trigger types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-triggers.html)

question: For a Release record, what options are available in the Release phase list?

options.label: A
options.text: Requirement Gathering, Design, Build, Roll-out, Unit Testing, User Acceptance, Pilot

options.label: B
options.text: Scoping, Design, Develop, Deployment, Unit Testing, Integration, Pilot

options.label: C
options.text: Analyze, Design, Development, Build, Roll-out, QA, User Acceptance

options.label: D
options.text: Requirement Gathering, Design, Development, Build, Deployment, QA, User Acceptance

explanation:
The baseline Release phase choices are Requirement Gathering, Design, Development, Build, Deployment, QA, and User Acceptance. ServiceNow Release Management supports defining phases that represent the stages of work for a release.

**Learn more:** [Using Release Management v2](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/release-management/c_Release.html)

question: Which of the following can be defined through step-based fulfillment in Catalog Builder? (select 2)
explanation:
Catalog Builder’s step-based fulfillment supports Task, Custom approval, and Manager approval step types in the base system. Therefore, approvals and tasks can be defined as fulfillment steps.

**Learn more:** [Define a service fulfillment step](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/create-sf-step.html?contentId=bIz4rCLqmg8uK7RbjRJCmg) · [Create a service fulfillment step type](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/create-sf-step-type.html)

question: Category and Subcategory values may be configured manually on the Incident form. What are the disadvantages of this method? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Too many options may confuse users and increase mis-categorization

options.label: B
options.text: Choices have no additional metadata to drive process

options.label: D
options.text: It is not part of the baseline instance

explanation:
Static manual choice values can become numerous, which can confuse users and lead to incorrect categorization. They also do not provide additional metadata that can be used to drive process behavior. ServiceNow documents Category and Subcategory as configurable Incident choices and notes that baseline categories and subcategories exist and can be used in assignment rules and notifications.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Incident categories and subcategories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/r_CategorizingIncidents.html) · [ServiceNow: Configure incident category or subcategory](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/t_AddRemoveIncCatSubbCat.html)

question: In release management, what governs the state transition from Scoping to Awaiting Approval?
explanation: A state model governs the lifecycle of a record by defining its states and the permitted transitions between those states. Workflows and flows can automate work associated with a transition, but the state model controls whether the transition from Scoping to Awaiting Approval is valid.

question: When you create a catalog, which field identifies who can create, modify, and publish items in that catalog?
explanation: The Editors field defines the users who have permission to create, modify, and publish items within the catalog.

question: By default, when using Inbound actions, what occurs if an email is received that contains an Incident watermark?

options.label: B
options.text: Incident record is updated, per the action's script

options.label: C
options.text: Auto-reply sent to sender, recommending they use Portal chat

options.label: D
options.text: Incident record is re-set to state = attention required

explanation:
An Incident watermark identifies an existing Incident record. The default inbound email action updates that existing Incident according to the action’s script.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Inbound email actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_InboundEmailActions.html)

question: In the baseline Change - Normal model, when a Change request moves to the Review state, what occurs to implementation and testing tasks that have not been closed?

options.label: C
options.text: They are automatically assigned to the Change assignee and closed

options.label: D
options.text: An error displays, requiring that the Tasks be closed before moving to Review

explanation:
In the baseline normal-change workflow, moving into Review automatically cancels any still-open implementation and testing tasks. Cancellation is the appropriate state for tasks that are no longer required, whereas closing indicates that a task was completed.

**Learn more:** [Create a change task](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-a-change-task.html) · [Change types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/change-types.html)

question: Which state transition will a General Problem record move through automatically when the required fields have been completed?

options.label: D
options.text: Root Cause Analysis to Fix in Progress

explanation:
A General Problem record automatically moves from New to Assess when the mandatory fields required for the Assess state have been completed. Subsequent lifecycle transitions require workflow actions rather than occurring solely from completing the initial required fields.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/it-service-management/problem-management/create-a-problem-v2.html)

question: When using the baseline business rule, **Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO**, which behaviors would you expect on an Incident form? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: If selected CI does not have an Owner group, write the Support group from the Service Offering to the Assignment group field

options.label: B
options.text: If selected CI has a Support group, write that group to the Assignment group field

options.label: C
options.text: If selected CI has an Owner group, write that group to the Assignment group field

options.label: D
options.text: If selected CI does not have a Support group, write the Support group from the Service Offering to the Assignment group field

explanation:
For Incidents, the rule populates Assignment group from the selected configuration item’s Support group. If the CI has no Support group, it uses the Support group on the Service Offering instead. The default Incident configuration does not use the CI Owner group for this assignment.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create an incident](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-it-service-management/page/product/incident-management/task/create-an-incident.html)

question: When using Catalog Builder, which items can be created from templates? (select 2)
explanation:
Catalog Builder supports templates for standard catalog items and for record producers. A template can predefine or restrict attributes used when creating either type of item.

**Learn more:** [Creating or editing catalog item template](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/create-cat-item-template-cat-builder.html)

question: Which of the following specifies the approvals that should be applied to a change request?
explanation:
A Change Approval Policy is applied to a change request and evaluates policy decisions to determine which associated approval definitions apply. It therefore defines the approvals required for the request.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Change approval policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/change-approval-policy.html)

question:
On the native ServiceNow platform, the service catalog is available through the **Self-Service > Service Catalog** module. Your customer wants to modify this home page by adding, removing, and rearranging the categories.

Which roles allow users to make these edits? (select 2)
explanation:
The `catalog_admin` role can manage the Service Catalog application, including its catalogs, categories, and items. The `admin` role has access to all system features and functions, so it can also administer and reorganize Service Catalog categories.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/roles-by-product/roles_servicecatalog.html) · [Base system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/r_BaseSystemRoles.html?contentId=CicEKXNxTK1BP0BaqtAhuw)

question: Which process is responsible for delivering items that were ordered through a Service Catalog?
explanation:
Catalog fulfillment handles a catalog request after an item is ordered, including approvals, assignment of fulfillment tasks, and completion of the request. Workflows or flows can define and automate the fulfillment process, but fulfillment is the process that delivers the ordered item.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog request fulfillment](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/request-fulfillment.html)

question: Where can an administrator view every search query that users enter in Knowledge search?
explanation:
ServiceNow’s Knowledge Search Log stores the history of all Knowledge searches users perform, including the search term and the user who performed it. Administrators and knowledge managers access it through Knowledge > Administration > Search Log. The log displays records from the Knowledge Searches (`ts_query_kb`) table; it is not the `kb_view` or `kb_feedback` table. This logging applies to Zing searches, not AI Search. 

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Search Log fields and description](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/km-search-logs.html)

question: Which platform role is able to create service portfolios and taxonomy nodes?
explanation:
The `portfolio_admin` role has administrative permissions to create and manage service portfolios and taxonomy levels or nodes. ServiceNow identifies `portfolio_admin` as the required role for both creating portfolios and creating taxonomy nodes.

**Learn more:** [Create portfolios in Service Portfolio Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-portfolio-management/create-or-modify-SPM2-portfolios.html?contentId=J8XXhAnX4~8lZp1Qpv3t7w) · [Create taxonomy nodes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-portfolio-management/create-or-mod-SPM2-taxonomy-nodes.html)

question: Which tools can an assignee use to help resolve an Incident? *(select 2)*
explanation: Known Errors provide documented root causes and workarounds, while resolutions from similar incidents let an assignee reuse prior successful fixes. Both directly support incident resolution.

question:
You have just released a new Change Model to the testers. The testers report that they can view the old change models but cannot view the new change model on the change landing page.

What could be causing this?

options.label: A
options.text: Testers need itil role to see the change models

options.label: B
options.text: New change model needs Active to be set to True

options.label: C
options.text: New change models are only visible to Change Managers

explanation:
An inactive Change Model is unavailable for selection when creating a change request. Setting **Active** to `True` makes the model available; therefore, an inactive new model can be missing while existing active models remain visible. ServiceNow also documents a separate “Available in 'Create New'” setting for availability on the Models tab, but that setting is not represented by the listed choices.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a Change model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-a-change-model.html?contentId=sDV0MpBQ8JbbqmWaKxCh_w)

question: When you create a catalog, which field identifies who can edit, update, and delete catalogs, categories, and catalog items?
explanation:
The **Manager** field assigns the catalog manager, who can manage the catalog and its associated categories and catalog items. The manager can also assign editors and change the catalog manager, unlike an editor, who cannot change the manager.

**Learn more:** [Multiple service catalogs setup](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_MultipleServiceCatalogs.html)

question: What occurs when an existing service record is checked out for editing in Service Builder?

options.label: A
options.text: The service portfolio record is placed in a Work in progress state

options.label: B
options.text: The service and offerings are temporarily unavailable for consumption

options.label: C
options.text: A copy of the service is created and placed in a Draft state

options.label: D
options.text: The original service record is placed in a Retired state

explanation: Checking out a service creates an editable copy in the Draft state while preserving the existing service record and its currently consumable offerings.

question: A customer wants to add a notification to the Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow. What should you do first to fulfill this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a copy of the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow, and then edit the new copy

options.label: B
options.text: Create a backup of the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow, and edit the baseline flow

options.label: C
options.text: Deactivate the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow

options.label: D
options.text: Unpublish the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow

explanation:
Provided Change Management flows are read-only so they can be upgraded. Custom behavior must be implemented in a copied flow, preserving the baseline flow as the upgradeable original.

**Learn more:** [Solved: How to Activate flow?](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-forum/how-to-activate-flow/m-p/3497809)

question: Which of the following roles can create and manage user criteria for service catalogs?
explanation:
The `catalog_admin` role can create and manage Service Catalog user criteria records. Catalog managers and catalog editors may apply existing criteria to assigned items and categories, but they cannot create or edit user criteria directly.

**Learn more:** [Set security for items and categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogAccessControls.html?contentId=BBdRyIVGM9TSYRfdePUqRA) · [Create a user criteria record in Service Catalog](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateAUserCriteriaRecord.html)

question: Which Incident Management roles are activated when the ITSM Roles plugin (`com.snc.itsm.roles`) is installed? (select 2)
explanation:
The ITSM Roles—Incident Management plugin introduces granular access roles for Incident Management: `sn_incident_read` grants read access and `sn_incident_write` grants write access. `incident_manager` is an existing role with added responsibilities, not one of these newly activated granular roles.

**Learn more:** [Request ITSM Roles — Incident Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/req-itsm-roles-inci-mgmt.html?contentId=QQZqGpQYJV3wiErXkUV0Ow) · [Components installed with ITSM Roles — Incident Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/inci-roles-instld-itsm-roles.html)

question: Which of the following can use user criteria to control access? (select 2)
explanation:
In ServiceNow Service Catalog, user criteria can be applied to catalog items and categories through their Available For and Not Available For related lists, determining which users can access each item or category.

**Learn more:** [Apply user criteria to items and categories](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_AppUserCritItemsCat.html)

question:
Your implementation team has a new Business Analyst. They will attend their first Service Catalog workshop and be responsible for recording notes and decisions from the workshop.

Which Now Create assets do you recommend they review to prepare? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Workshop Preparation Guide

options.label: B
options.text: Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Process Guide

options.label: C
options.text: IT Service Management - Typical Challenges and Remediation

options.label: D
options.text: ITSM - Business Outcomes and Corresponding KPIs

explanation: The Service Catalog and Request Management Workshop Preparation Guide prepares participants for the workshop, and the Service Catalog and Request Management Process Guide supplies the relevant process context for accurately capturing workshop discussions and decisions.

question: In which table are Change records stored?
explanation:
ServiceNow stores Change Request records in the `change_request` table. Change tasks are stored separately in `change_task` and are associated with a parent change request.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg)

question: By default, when using Inbound actions, what occurs when an email is received with an Incident watermark?

options.label: A
options.text: Incident record is set to state = on hold

options.label: C
options.text: Incident record is updated, per the action's script

options.label: D
options.text: Auto-reply sent to sender, recommending they use Portal chat

explanation:
An email containing a watermark for an existing Incident is associated with that Incident, and the inbound email action updates the existing record according to the action’s script.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Inbound email actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_InboundEmailActions.html)

question: Which record type should you use for an Ask a Question form that generates an Incident?
explanation: A Record Producer presents a form to users and creates a record in a target table, such as the Incident table, from the submitted values.

question: Which organizational role has responsibility for the overall administrative capabilities of a portfolio?
explanation: A Portfolio Manager performs the operational administration of a portfolio, including maintaining portfolio records and supporting its day-to-day management. Portfolio ownership is a strategic accountability role, whereas service roles apply to individual services.

question: Your customer wants to understand why users with the `problem_coordinator` role can communicate workarounds and fixes, whereas users with `problem_task_analyst` cannot. How do you explain this?

options.label: A
options.text: The technical resources working on the problem investigation are focused on the technical details, and may provide information that is not useful for the callers

options.label: B
options.text: The problem coordinator is the only role with the ability to recall a message

options.label: C
options.text: The problem coordinator is responsible for approving or rejecting the proposed message

options.label: D
options.text: The message will be automatically displayed on the Portal

explanation:
Problem-task analysts focus on the technical investigation and may provide details that are not useful to incident callers. The problem coordinator is the role authorized to communicate the customer-relevant workaround or fix to related incidents. ServiceNow documentation lists `problem_coordinator` among the roles required for both communication actions, but does not list `problem_task_analyst`.

**Learn more:** [Communicate workaround for Problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-workaround.html) · [Communicate a fix](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-a-fix.html)

question:
Risk is configured by default to calculate **Risk = High** for a change scheduled with only 3 days of lead time. Your customer’s change policy requires changes to be requested with 5 days of lead time.

How would you meet this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Update the Risk Property for Insufficient lead time

options.label: B
options.text: Update the Risk Assessment Matrix for Insufficient lead time

options.label: C
options.text: Update the Calculate Risk UI Action

options.label: D
options.text: Update the Risk Matrix for insufficient lead time

options.label: E
options.text: Update the Risk Condition for Insufficient lead time

explanation:
The Change Risk Calculator uses predefined risk conditions to calculate a change’s risk. The **Insufficient lead time** risk condition contains the lead-time criterion that triggers High risk, so its threshold must be changed from 3 days to 5 days. [ServiceNow: Risk conditions and calculation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/change-risk-assess-detect-conflict.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Risk conditions and calculation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/change-risk-assess-detect-conflict.html)

question: Where are the technical approvals, executed in the Change - Normal - Assess flow, defined?
explanation:
A Change Approval Policy contains the decisions and approval definitions that specify the approvals required for a change request. The flow applies that policy to generate and process the technical approvals.
