**Learn more:** [Change approval policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/change-approval-policy.html) · [Use the Apply Change Approval Policy flow action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/use-apply-change-approval-policy-flow-activity.html)

question: In a Normal Change Model, what are examples of the Model State Transitions defined for the Authorize state?

options.label: A
options.text: Authorize to Draft, Authorize to Assess, Authorize to Review

options.label: B
options.text: Authorize to Implement, Authorize to Assess, Authorize to Review

options.label: C
options.text: Authorize to Canceled, Authorize to New, Authorize to Scheduled

options.label: D
options.text: Authorize to Scheduled, Authorize to Closed, Authorize to New

explanation:
For a normal change, the Authorize state can transition to Scheduled after final authorization, to New when authorization is rejected, and to Canceled because cancellation is allowed before closure.

**Learn more:** [State model and transitions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-it-service-management/page/product/change-management/concept/c_ChangeStateModel.html) · [State progression for normal, standard, and emergency changes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/normal-standard-emergency-states.html)

question: A customer needs assistance defining Category values for Problem records. Which approaches should be recommended? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Re-use existing categories from legacy systems

options.label: B
options.text: Define categories based on the customer’s CMDB classes

options.label: C
options.text: Re-use existing categories from incident management

options.label: D
options.text: Define categories based on ITIL problem taxonomy

explanation: Problem categories should be consistent with incident-management categories so related records can be classified and reported coherently. They should also reflect CMDB classes to identify the affected technology or configuration-item type. ITIL provides process guidance but does not prescribe a fixed problem-category taxonomy.

question: Which module is a helpful starting point for a manager to view current-state operational information for Incident management?
explanation: The **Incident > Overview** module provides managers with a high-level operational view of the current Incident Management state, including incident status and performance information.

question: In which situation should you use the **Communicate workaround** related link on the Problem record?

options.label: A
options.text: The workaround is helpful information for the Callers on the Problem's related Incidents (open)

options.label: B
options.text: The workaround should be published to a knowledge article, visible from the portal

options.label: C
options.text: The workaround is helpful information for the members of the Problem's Assignment Group

options.label: D
options.text: The workaround is helpful information for the members of the Problem's Work notes list

explanation: The Communicate workaround action communicates a workaround to callers associated with the Problem’s related open Incidents, so affected users can apply it while the underlying issue is being resolved.

question: What is the minimum number of offering(s) that a service needs to have before moving to the Catalog phase?
explanation: A service must have at least one associated service offering to be moved to the Catalog phase, because the offering represents how the service is made available to consumers.

question: What is the relationship of Features to Products and Releases?

options.label: A
options.text: Emergency releases can include products and features

options.label: B
options.text: Products have associated features, which are organized into releases

options.label: C
options.text: Features are included in releases, not associated with products

options.label: D
options.text: Products use features to define release types

explanation: Products can have associated features, and releases organize those features into planned deliverables.

question: How is granular read and write access for a particular change model configured?

options.label: A
options.text: Configuring ACL's on the Create New landing page

options.label: B
options.text: Setting Advanced Security to true and applying user criteria

options.label: C
options.text: Configuring ACL’s on the chge_model table

explanation:
Granular, model-specific access is configured by enabling **Advanced Security** on the change model and applying user criteria. This exposes controls such as **Available For** for access and **Can Write** for editable access, allowing permissions to be tailored per model.

**Learn more:** [Create a Change model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-a-change-model.html?contentId=sDV0MpBQ8JbbqmWaKxCh_w) · [Create a user criteria record for Change Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-user-criteria.html)

question: What are the main relationships between Change Management and Release Management? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Release management application is required, to use the Change management application

options.label: B
options.text: Change includes planning and approvals; Release includes building, testing and execution of changes

options.label: C
options.text: A Release can contain one or more Changes

options.label: D
options.text: A Change can contain one or more Releases

options.label: E
options.text: Change management provides governance, which includes Release management

explanation:
Change Management supplies the governance framework, including planning and approvals, while Release Management organizes the build, testing, and execution/deployment of release work. A release can group and be associated with one or more change requests, whose implementation is handled through the change-management process.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Release Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/release-management/c_ITILReleaseManagement.html) · [ServiceNow Change Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/c_ITILChangeManagement.html)

question:
A customer wants to modify how **Priority** on Problem records is calculated from **Impact** and **Urgency**.

Which module should be used to find and update the **Priority Problem Lookup** record?
explanation:
Problem priority mapping based on Impact and Urgency is configured through the **Priority Problem Lookup** data lookup definition. The **Data Lookup Definitions** module is where that definition record is located and maintained.

**Learn more:** [Define priority lookup rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/def-prio-lookup-rules.html)

question: Which of the following can use user criteria to control access? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow user criteria control Service Catalog visibility by defining Available For and Not Available For access conditions on catalog categories and catalog items.

**Learn more:** [Create a category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateACategory.html) · [CatCategory - Scoped API reference](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_CatCategory.html)

question:
A key stakeholder for your ITSM implementation wants SLAs on every Task record.

What guidance do you provide about SLAs on Problem records?

options.label: A
options.text: SLAs are essential to problem management, as support specialists need to quickly identify root causes

options.label: B
options.text: SLAs may be counterproductive to problem management, as the key objective is to permanently fix an error no matter how long that may take

options.label: C
options.text: SLAs are available for problem management, but require custom code

options.label: D
options.text: SLAs are recommended in the ITIL framework for problem management

explanation: Problem management is intended to identify root causes and permanently remove errors. A resolution-time SLA can create pressure for short-term closure rather than a durable fix, so SLAs may be counterproductive for Problem records.

question: Which type of catalog item can be found in a Service Catalog?
explanation:
Order guides are a basic Service Catalog item type that groups multiple catalog items into one request. Requested items are request records, categories organize catalog content, and execution plans define fulfillment behavior rather than serving as catalog item types.

**Learn more:** [Types of catalog items](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/r_ExtendedCatalogItemFunctions.html)

question: What occurs when a user selects the **Communicate Workaround** UI action on the Problem form?

options.label: A
options.text: Workaround is written to the Comments field on any open Incident associated with the problem

options.label: B
options.text: Workaround is written to the Workaround field on any incident associated with the problem

options.label: C
options.text: Workaround is written to a draft Knowledge article

options.label: D
options.text: Workaround is written to the Work notes field on any open Incident associated with the problem

explanation:
The Communicate Workaround action copies the workaround from the Problem record to the **Work notes** of related open Incident records. ServiceNow documents that this communication applies to Incident records in active states such as New, On Hold, or In Progress.

**Learn more:** [Communicate workaround for Problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-workaround.html) · [Synchronization between incident and problem records](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-service-management/problem-management/sync-btwn-inci-prob.html)

question: How are the relationships between services and offerings created in Service Portfolio Management transferred to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)?

options.label: A
options.text: Only parent:child (service:offering) relationships are automatically created in the CMDB

options.label: B
options.text: If the service is defined as a business service, the relationships and dependencies will be automatically in the CMDB

options.label: C
options.text: All CMDB relationships and dependencies are automatically created upon publishing the service and offerings

options.label: D
options.text: Any required CMDB relationships and dependencies must be created manually

explanation:
Service Portfolio Management adds service offerings to the CMDB and automatically maintains the parent-child relationship from a service to its offering. Other CMDB dependencies and relationships are not all generated automatically merely by defining or publishing a service and its offerings.

**Learn more:** [Service Portfolio Management activation administration](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-portfolio-management/SPM2-administration.html) · [Service Consumption domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/sell-consume-domain.html)

question: Which two measures effectively evaluate the performance of the Problem Management process? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Problems older than 30 days by Priority and State

options.label: B
options.text: Number of Problem that have Breached SLAs

options.label: C
options.text: Percentage of Problem Resolution within SLA by Category

explanation:
Problem Management performance can be measured by the aging and status of open problems, segmented by priority, because it reveals backlog and stalled work. Average Problem Resolution Time measures the speed at which problems are closed. ServiceNow’s Problem dashboard includes open problems by age and priority/state and mean time to close a problem as KPIs. Service level agreements are not recommended for an overall problem because investigation and remediation can be long-term efforts.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Problem dashboard](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem.html) · [ServiceNow Problem Management process](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/c_ProblemManagementProcess.html)

question: What specifies the required approvals and their associated conditions for a change model?
explanation: A change model approval definition specifies the approvals required for a change model and the conditions that control when those approvals apply.

question: Which capability gives visibility into data joined across multiple tables?
explanation:
Database Views define table joins and combine data from multiple tables into a single reportable source. [ServiceNow documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_CreatingDatabaseViews.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Joining tables using database views](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_CreatingDatabaseViews.html)

question: Which module is used to modify the setting for the time between incident resolution and closure?
explanation:
The incident auto-close delay is configured in **Incident Properties** through the property that specifies the number of days after which resolved incidents are automatically closed (`glide.ui.autoclose.time`). ServiceNow locates this configuration under Incident > Administration > Incident Properties.

**Learn more:** [Configure incidents to close automatically](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/configure-incident-auto-close.html) · [Incident Management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/incident-management-properties.html)

question: A user asks what distinguishes the Known Error knowledge base in ServiceNow from every other knowledge base. How should you respond?

options.label: A
options.text: The Known Error knowledge base documents problems that are under investigation, but not yet have a root cause

options.label: B
options.text: Only users with sn_known_error_write can create Known Error articles

options.label: C
options.text: Users with sn_problem_write can create known error articles, but not articles for other knowledge bases

options.label: D
options.text: The Known Error knowledge articles use a template, which includes the Workaround and the Cause

explanation:
Known Error articles use a specialized template that includes fields for the workaround and the cause. ServiceNow documents these fields on the Known Error article form, with the workaround describing how to overcome the problem and the cause recording what caused it.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Known error article form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/known-error-article-form.html?contentId=xuTxK_uRvVxt0WAfPfg8Ag)

question: Which key relationships exist between Changes and Incidents? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Incidents autoclose upon closure of a related Change

options.label: B
options.text: Incidents can be caused by a Change

options.label: D
options.text: Incident owners are part of the change approval workflow

explanation:
A Change can be linked to incidents that its implementation caused, and it can be linked to incidents that require that Change for resolution. ServiceNow provides related lists for both **Incidents Caused by Change** and **Incidents Fixed by Change**.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Create a change request](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/t_CreateAChange.html)

question: Which tools can an assignee use to help resolve an Incident? (select 2)
explanation: Knowledge Articles provide documented resolution guidance, and Workarounds provide alternative steps that can restore service or mitigate an incident while a permanent fix is developed.

question: Which configuration item field automatically populates an incident record’s **Assignment group** field?
explanation:
A configuration item’s **Support group** identifies the group responsible for supporting that CI and is used to route incidents by populating the incident Assignment group. ServiceNow documentation describes support groups associated with configuration items in incident workflows.

**Learn more:** [On-call support for an incident in Service Operations Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/on-call-sow.html)

question: Which role is needed to accept a Major Incident?
explanation:
In ServiceNow Major Incident Management, accepting a major incident candidate requires the `major_incident_manager` role. [ServiceNow documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/accept-reject-major-incident-candidate.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Accept or reject a major incident candidate](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/accept-reject-major-incident-candidate.html)

question: By default, a business rule automatically sets the **Assignment group**. How is the group determined?

options.label: A
options.text: Change group on CI record, or if empty, the Change group on the Service offering

options.label: B
options.text: Support group on CI record, or the default assignment group for the user

options.label: C
options.text: Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service

options.label: D
options.text: Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service offering

explanation:
ServiceNow’s out-of-box **Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO** business rule populates the assignment group from the configuration item’s support group, falling back to the service offering’s support group when necessary.

**Learn more:** [Create an incident — ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/it-service-management/incident-management/create-an-incident.html)

question: Which of the following cannot be configured or set by using a Catalog UI Policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply a requirement to all form views

options.label: C
options.text: Reverse UI Policy if conditions are false

explanation:
Catalog UI Policies can set catalog variables to mandatory or read-only and can reverse actions when catalog conditions evaluate to false. They apply to catalog items or variable sets and designated catalog/request contexts, not to all form views.

**Learn more:** [Service catalog UI policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogUIPolicy.html) · [UI policy form in Catalog Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/ui-policy-form-in-catalog-builder.html)

question: Which actions may a user with the `itil_admin` role perform in support of Change Management? (select 3)
explanation:
The `itil_admin` Change Management permissions include administering risk assessments, administering risk conditions used for risk calculation, and deleting change request records. Deleting a CAB definition requires the broader system `admin` privilege, and creating or editing Change Approval Policies requires `change_manager` or `admin` permissions rather than `itil_admin`.

**Learn more:** [Create approval definitions — ServiceNow Product Documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-approval-definitions.html) · [Create a CAB definition — ServiceNow Product Documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/define-your-cab.html)

question:
On a request form, the requester must indicate the date by which they need to receive the item.

Which Variable type would you use for this information?
explanation:
A Date variable captures a requested calendar date and provides a field with a calendar for selecting that date. A delivery-needed-by value is a date, not a duration or a separately named date-picker variable type.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Date, Date and time, and Duration](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/date.html)

question: Which Knowledge base feature can you use to standardize the sections and fonts in a knowledge article?
explanation:
Knowledge article templates provide reusable, standardized article structures and can be customized to control the presentation of article content, including section layout and font styling.

**Learn more:** [Knowledge article templates](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/knowledge-article-templates.html?contentId=Zyboo4Jq7WphiA8vmMS4~A) · [Create an article template and use it to create a knowledge article](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/create-a-new-article-templates.html)

question: In the baseline implementation, which key relationships exist between Change and Configuration Item (CI) records? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: The CI Manager is part of the change approval workflow

options.label: B
options.text: One Change can be submitted for multiple CIs

options.label: C
options.text: Changes should reference at least one CI

options.label: D
options.text: The CI Support Group is responsible for change implementations

options.label: E
options.text: A CI can be affected by a change, even if it is not the CI being changed

explanation:
A change request is used to control modifications to supported configuration items and should identify a CI. A change can have a primary CI plus multiple associated affected or impacted CIs. Therefore, an affected CI does not have to be the primary CI to which the change directly applies. CI ownership fields do not, by themselves, make the CI manager an approver or the CI support group responsible for implementation.

**Learn more:** [Associated CIs on a change request](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/c_AffectedCIsAndImpactedServices.html) · [Create a change request](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/t_CreateAChange.html)

question: When a Service Desk shares a "How to" item with a customer again, what type of record is being shared?
explanation:
ServiceNow Knowledge Management stores and distributes instructional self-service guidance as knowledge articles. A “How to” designation identifies the instructional nature of the content, while the underlying record remains a knowledge article.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Zurich release notes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/release-notes/rn-summary-new-features.html?contentId=nnZXhdGARFA~ooNjb_cIig)

question: What determines which catalog items are included in an Order Guide, and the order in which they are included?
explanation:
Order guide rules specify the catalog item to include when their conditions are met. A rule’s position setting controls its placement, so rules determine both inclusion and ordering of catalog items in an Order Guide.

**Learn more:** [Create an order guide rule to add a catalog item](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateARule.html)

question: Unless specific security requirements apply, which role is assigned to users who carry out request-fulfillment work?
explanation:
ServiceNow's out-of-box Request Management configuration assigns the 'fulfiller' role to users responsible for carrying out request-fulfillment tasks (working request items and catalog tasks), reserving the broader 'itil' role and other specialized roles for cases where additional security restrictions on ITSM data are required.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Docs — IT Service Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/it-service-management/r_ITServiceManagement.html)

question: When creating multiple catalog items, which components should be assessed for consolidation and reuse? (select 2)
explanation:
Variable sets package common catalog variables so they can be attached to multiple catalog items and order guides. Reusable subflows centralize shared fulfillment or approval logic, allowing multiple flows to invoke the same operations instead of duplicating them.

**Learn more:** [Create a variable set and add it to an item](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateAVariableSet.html) · [General guidelines for flows and subflows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/design-considerations-consolidated.html)

question: Which catalog item type should be used to create an incident record through the portal?
explanation: A Record Producer is a ServiceNow catalog item that creates a record in a target table, such as the Incident table, from a portal-facing form.

question: What should be used to capture data in a grid-style layout on a catalog item?
explanation: A multi-row variable set provides a repeatable, table-like set of variables, allowing requesters to enter multiple rows of structured data on a catalog item.

question:
A customer requires every Cloud Infrastructure change that involves a Critical CI to pass through a Review state. They have duplicated the baseline Cloud Infrastructure base model.

Which additional configuration is needed to meet this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Modify the default Cloud Infrastructure flow

options.label: B
options.text: Add Review State for critical CI's

options.label: C
options.text: Add the Critical CI field to the CI record form

options.label: D
options.text: Add the Review state to the model record

options.label: E
options.text: Add the Critical CI field to the Change Request form

explanation:
Change models define the state model and state transitions for their change requests. A copied Cloud Infrastructure model must include the Review state in its own model-state configuration for changes using that model to enter Review; form-field changes and the baseline flow do not add a lifecycle state to the copied model.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Change models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/UMl~97STJe3fa_KTmzD1Gg/TulaQ1sDsIrBvKmcr1PFwA) · [ServiceNow Legacy: State model and transitions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/c_ChangeStateModel.html)

question: Roles determine which users may perform particular actions on a change record. Which actions cannot be performed by anyone, including an administrator? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Update Change Type on an existing change record

explanation:
ServiceNow treats the change type as a process-defining attribute: it selects the applicable state model and required change process, so it cannot be changed after the change record is created. Standard change templates have a controlled lifecycle in which they can be modified or retired (deactivated), not deleted. By contrast, ServiceNow documentation explicitly permits authorized users, including administrators, to delete change records.

**Learn more:** [Change types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/change-types.html) · [Modify or retire a standard change template](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/manage-standard-change-template.html)

question: How would you characterize the relationship between a Knowledge article and a Knowledge base category?

options.label: A
options.text: Articles can only be published to one category

options.label: B
options.text: Articles must be published to at least one category

options.label: C
options.text: Articles must be approved by the selected category owner

options.label: D
options.text: Articles can be published to a category and subcategory

explanation:
A Knowledge article can be assigned a category and, optionally, a subcategory within that category hierarchy. ServiceNow documents category selection for articles and explicitly provides the optional step to select or add a subcategory.

**Learn more:** [Select a knowledge article category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_SelectACategory.html) · [Define a knowledge article category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/t_DefineAKnowledgeCategory.html)

question: Where are the time-frame conditions for sending an SLA breach-warning notification defined?
explanation:
SLA breach-warning notification timing is controlled by the Default SLA flow, which defines the notification events and their threshold timing during an SLA’s progression. SLA definitions provide the SLA duration and lifecycle configuration, while the flow determines when warning and breach notifications are sent.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: SLA notifications](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-level-management/c_SLANotifications.html) · [ServiceNow: Service Level Agreement (SLA) definition](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-level-management/c_SLADefinitions.html?contentId=9U~s0ZIeKnZzzMG0GOXyTQ)

question: When a user selects the **Communicate fix** UI action on the Problem form, what occurs?

options.label: A
options.text: Fix is written to the Comments field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is On Hold, Awaiting Problem

options.label: B
options.text: Fix is written to the Work notes field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is Active

options.label: C
options.text: Fix is written to the Comments field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is Active

options.label: D
options.text: Fix is written to a draft Knowledge article

explanation:
The Communicate Fix action copies the Problem record’s fix information to the **Work notes** field of related active Incident records, allowing the incident-assignment team to receive the fix details.

**Learn more:** [Synchronization between incident and problem records](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/it-service-management/problem-management/sync-btwn-inci-prob.html)

question: Which baseline Change Flows support the baseline Normal Change model?

options.label: A
options.text: Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Authorize, Change - Normal - Implement Change - Implementation tasks

options.label: B
options.text: Change - Normal - New, Change - Normal - Review, Change - Normal - Close, Change - Implementation tasks

options.label: C
options.text: Change - Normal - New, Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Implement, Change - Implementation tasks

options.label: D
options.text: Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Authorize, Change - Normal - Close, Change - Implementation tasks

explanation:
The baseline Normal Change model is supported by flows for the Assess, Authorize, and Implement states, along with the Change - Implementation tasks flow that creates and waits for implementation and post-implementation tasks.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Change flows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/it-service-management/change-management/change-flows.html)

question:
A company that sells bicycles wants to create a service catalog for existing and prospective customers so they can browse bicycles and accessories and make purchases.

Which interface is appropriate for these external users?
explanation:
Customer Service Catalog is intended for external customer self-service. It can expose catalog items through customer-facing portals, enabling customers and consumers to browse catalog offerings and submit requests or purchases. [ServiceNow: Request an item or service from the Customer Service Portal](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/customer-service-management/customer-request-from-portal.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Request an item or service from the Customer Service Portal](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/customer-service-management/customer-request-from-portal.html) · [ServiceNow — Service catalog integration with the Customer and Consumer Service Portals](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/customer-service-management/service-catalog-request-integration.html)

question: Which Agent Workspace feature automatically provides agents with search results that suggest possible solutions for records they open?
explanation:
Agent Assist in ServiceNow Agent Workspace provides contextual assistance by automatically surfacing relevant search results and possible resolutions for the record an agent is viewing. Related Search Results is a component or display area used for such results, whereas Agent Assist is the feature that delivers the automated assistance.

**Learn more:** [Similar case recommendations](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/customer-service-management/customer-service-similar-cases.html)

question:
A problem record’s current status is tracked in the **State** field. Every state has a label, value, and constant. The following example is for the **Fix in Progress** state:

- Label: Fix in Progress
- Value: 104
- Constant: `Problem State STATES.FIX IN PROGRESS`

Your customer wants to add a prerequisite for moving out of the **Fix in Progress** state. When updating the script include, which value is better to use in the script?
explanation:
A named state constant is preferable to a hard-coded numeric value or display label because it is readable, expresses the intended lifecycle state, and remains resilient when the underlying state value or label is changed. `ProblemState.STATES.FIX_IN_PROGRESS` is the constant representing the Fix in Progress state.

**Learn more:** [Map problem states](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/map-problem-state.html?contentId=weSiKxt_VEi0duc4JAC1yQ)

question: What is typically done when a Root Cause and a Workaround have been identified for a problem, in order to document the fastest known resolution?
explanation: A known error record documents a problem whose root cause is understood and whose workaround provides the quickest known way to restore service while a permanent fix is pursued.

question: What occurs when an agent hovers over the reference icon beside the caller field on an incident record, if no `sys_popup` view is defined for the `[sys_user]` table?

options.label: A
options.text: The default view of the User form is displayed

options.label: C
options.text: Only dot-walked fields will be displayed

options.label: D
options.text: There will be no reference icon if there is no sys_popup defined

explanation:
A reference icon’s hover pop-up uses the referenced table’s `sys_popup` view when one is defined. If no `sys_popup` view exists, ServiceNow uses the table’s default view, so the default User form view is displayed.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Reference field icon](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_ReferenceIcon.html)

question: A customer needs incidents to automatically transition from **Resolved** to **Closed** after 7 days. How should this be configured? *(select 2)*

options.label: A
options.text: Configure the incident lifecycle flow script action

options.label: B
options.text: Configure the number of days Resolved incidents automatically close property

options.label: C
options.text: Configure the incident lifecycle timeline property

options.label: D
options.text: Enable the auto closure of Incidents based on Resolution date property

explanation:
ServiceNow auto-closes resolved incidents according to the configured duration in the **Number of days Resolved incidents automatically close** property. Enabling **auto closure of Incidents based on Resolution date** makes the auto-close calculation use the incident’s resolution date rather than its last updated date.

**Learn more:** [Configure incidents to close automatically](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/configure-incident-auto-close.html) · [Incident Management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/incident-management-properties.html)

question: Your client wants a method to designate VIP callers on an incident form. How would you accomplish this?
explanation: A VIP Flag field style can conditionally apply visual formatting to the Caller field when the referenced user is marked as a VIP, making VIP callers identifiable on incident records.

question: Which tools are available to an assignee to assist with resolving an incident? (select 2)
explanation:
Workarounds provide a temporary means to restore service when a permanent fix is not yet available. Similar resolved incidents supply relevant prior resolutions that can support investigation and resolution of the current incident.

**Learn more:** [Recommendation rules for an incident in Service Operations Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/Recj91eIo1YnsOabQjgskg/~Dng3fcyivqMZQFwp9a1BQ) · [Communicate workaround for Problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-workaround.html)

question: After an Item is published through Catalog Builder, to which state is the associated update set set?
explanation:
Publishing a Catalog Builder item finalizes its automatically created update set for transfer between instances. ServiceNow identifies these as completed update sets, so the update set state is Complete.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Transfer catalog items using update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/transfer-catalog-items-using-update-sets.html)

question: At what level can a knowledge-feedback type be enabled or disabled?
explanation: Knowledge feedback types are configured at the knowledge-base level, which determines the feedback options available for articles within that knowledge base.

question: Which user roles can communicate a workaround or fix? (select 2)
explanation:
The Problem Management communication action is authorized for the `problem_manager` and `problem_admin` roles (as well as `admin` and `problem_coordinator`). A problem task analyst is not authorized for this action, and `itil_admin` is not the `admin` role.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Communicate workaround for Problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-workaround.html)

question:
A customer wants to add a requirement to the Normal Change Model. Before moving the change status from New to Assess, they want to ensure that the associated Configuration Item (CI) has a Proposed Change specified on its CI record.

What is the recommended way to implement this requirement?

options.label: B
options.text: Add a state transition condition to the state transition record "New to Assess"

options.label: C
options.text: Create a flow in Flow Designer for the new phase for the normal change model

explanation:
A state transition condition on the existing New-to-Assess transition can enforce that the required Proposed Change value is present on the associated CI before the change is allowed to enter Assess. ServiceNow state transitions are designed to control permitted state changes and apply required transition conditions; modifying an SNC script include is not the recommended extension point.

**Learn more:** [State Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/state-management/state-model.html?contentId=Sci5ySH9WhO6ArPvfduu5g) · [Create predefined transition condition types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-predefined-transition-condition-type.html)

question: Within a flow, you can automate a task by using a sequence of related steps, such as looking up a record, creating a record, or applying a policy. What is this flow component called?
explanation:
In ServiceNow Flow Designer, an action automates a repeatable task or operation within a flow by running a sequence of steps. Individual steps perform reusable operations such as looking up or creating records.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Exploring actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/exploring-actions.html)

question: What different methods can a user use to find items in a service catalog? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Use the search on catalog or portal

options.label: C
options.text: Use the Top Request or Popular Items widget

explanation: Service catalog items can be found either by using the catalog or portal search function or by browsing through the category hierarchy. The application navigator does not navigate catalog items, and Top Requests or Popular Items widgets only surface featured items rather than providing a general item-location method.

question: What benefits does problem management provide to incident management? (select 2)

options.label: B
options.text: Published workarounds help quickly resolve incidents

options.label: C
options.text: Problem investigations automatically triggered for multiple user incidents

explanation: Problem management reduces future incidents by resolving their underlying causes, and its published workarounds allow incidents to be resolved more quickly.

question: A customer reports that, when users select the Configuration Item magnifier on the Incident form, they are overwhelmed by the number of CIs available. They want to exclude particular CI types from the CI lists on the Incident, Problem, and Change forms. What do you recommend to the customer?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a Show field to the base cmdb table: Check the Show box on those CI records they want to display; make reference qualifier to display only the CIs with show=true

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Principal CI class checkbox, to identify the CI classes that they want visible on the Incident, Problem, and Change forms

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Access control to hide the unnecessary CIs from the itil users

options.label: D
options.text: Make a show/hide UI action to show only the desired CIs to the itil users

explanation:
Principal CI classes define which CI classes are in scope for incident, problem, and change processes. Designating only the appropriate classes as principal applies an automatic filter to the Configuration Item field on task records, reducing the CI choices users see without restricting access to CMDB records.

**Learn more:** [About principal classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-sa-principal-class.html?contentId=nk0aGrT2B9a3fxMVcFK88Q)

question: Request fulfillment uses three record types: Requests, Requested Items, and Catalog Tasks. The lifecycle status of these records is represented by a combination of state and stage fields. Which status field is set by the flow?
explanation:
For a flow that uses a Service Catalog trigger, Workflow Studio writes the current flow stage to the **Stage** field on the Requested Items (`sc_req_item`) table. State fields track the operational state of request, requested-item, and catalog-task records separately.

**Learn more:** [Configure stages and add them to a flow](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/add-stages.html)

question: Why do Problem records not automatically transition from **Resolved** to **Closed** after a fix has been implemented?

options.label: A
options.text: It is designed to follow the ITIL4 standard

options.label: B
options.text: There is a scheduled job that automatically moves Resolved problems to Closed after 7 days

options.label: C
options.text: There is no Closed state. Problem records are moved to Completed

options.label: D
options.text: It is good practice to monitor fixes implemented, to ensure the underlying issues are resolved, before closing a problem record

explanation:
A fix may require a monitoring period to verify that it has eliminated the underlying issue and has not caused recurrence or other unintended effects. A Problem record should therefore remain Resolved until the effectiveness of the fix is confirmed before it is closed. ServiceNow’s Problem Management lifecycle treats resolving and completing (closing) a problem as separate actions.

**Learn more:** [Resolve and complete a problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-it-service-management/page/product/problem-management/task/resolve-and-complete-problem.html)

question: What determines the class and table structure to which infrastructure configuration items map in the CSDM model?

options.label: A
options.text: The version number and type of CSDM implementation

options.label: B
options.text: The data sources, discovery tools, and system integrations

options.label: C
options.text: The selected CMDB domain and base system configuration

options.label: D
options.text: The user permissions and assigned administrative roles

explanation:
Infrastructure CI class and table mappings are driven by the data being brought into the CMDB and by the Discovery and integration mechanisms that identify or import those infrastructure types. ServiceNow Discovery patterns and Service Graph Connectors populate relevant CMDB classes, while CSDM provides the model for placing CI data in the appropriate tables.

**Learn more:** [CMDB schema model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ConfigurationManagementDatabase.html) · [Exploring the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-content-frame-exploring.html)

question:
A customer wants to restrict the users who can view internal Network requests to members of the Network department.

Which roles let you make these required changes? (select 2)
explanation:
A department-based user criterion limits catalog-item visibility to users whose Department is Network. The `user_criteria_admin` role administers those user criteria, and `catalog_editor` can modify the relevant catalog item in an assigned category to apply the restriction. `catalog_manager` and `catalog_admin` provide broader catalog-management privileges than necessary.

**Learn more:** [Base system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/r_BaseSystemRoles.html) · [User criteria form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-criteria-form-notifications.html)

question: Which field on a Catalog record identifies the person who can administer its categories?
explanation:
The **Manager** field assigns the catalog manager, who can edit and update the service catalog along with its categories and catalog items.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Multiple service catalogs setup](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_MultipleServiceCatalogs.html)

question: A tester reports a defect because they submitted a Known Error article from a Problem record, but it is not visible in the Known Error database. What could be causing this?

options.label: A
options.text: The article is in draft state, but has not been published

options.label: B
options.text: The Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin has not been activated

options.label: C
options.text: The user criteria on the knowledge base is incorrect

options.label: D
options.text: The tester is not impersonating an itil user

explanation:
Known Error articles created from Problem records are saved in the knowledge base and are governed by that knowledge base’s publishing workflow. An article that remains in Draft has not been published and is therefore not available in the Known Error database. [ServiceNow: Create a known error article](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/create-known-error-from-problem.html?contentId=~IWCVufjGM_NE5dwNPVEMQ)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a known error article](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/create-known-error-from-problem.html?contentId=~IWCVufjGM_NE5dwNPVEMQ)

question: What can be configured in the Unauthorized Change Properties module? (select 2)

options.label: B
options.text: Maximum number of unauthorized change records for a CI

explanation:
Unauthorized Change Properties can enable or disable the creation of unauthorized change requests when an unplanned CI-change event occurs, and its CI class inclusion setting selects the CI classes to monitor. [ServiceNow: Unauthorized change properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/unauth-change-properties.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Unauthorized change properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/unauth-change-properties.html)

question:
During request fulfillment, approvals may be required before a request can be fulfilled. Your customer is concerned that requests could become stuck in the process flow when an approver is away from the office for an extended period.

What can you recommend to address this concern? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: The approver can use the Delegate module to assign a person to approve on their behalf, while they are away from the office

options.label: B
options.text: The approver can set their approval notifications to forward to their personal email address

options.label: C
options.text: The approval can be defined as a group approval, where any member of the group can approve

options.label: D
options.text: The approver can set their approval notifications to auto-reply with “approved” in the subject line

explanation:
Service delegation lets an approver designate another user to view and act on approvals during an absence. A group approval can also be configured with logic that allows any member of the approver group to approve, preventing a single unavailable individual from blocking fulfillment.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Service Delegation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/self-service/c_ServiceDelegation.html) · [ServiceNow: Approval - Group workflow activity](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/workflow-activities/r_ApprovalGroup.html)

question: What is the key difference between an Incident and a Problem?

options.label: A
options.text: Incidents are focused on one individual having an issue; Problems are when you have many people having the same issue

options.label: B
options.text: Incidents can be any priority; Problems are high or critical

options.label: C
options.text: Incidents are the same as a Problem

options.label: D
options.text: Incidents are focused on the quickest resolution; Problems are focused on root cause analysis

explanation:
Incident management is intended to restore service quickly, whereas problem management identifies and resolves the underlying root cause to prevent recurring incidents. ServiceNow describes problem management as the ITIL process for finding and fixing root causes, while an incident can be resolved through a temporary workaround or permanent solution.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Incident resolution and closure](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/c_IncidentResolutionAndRecovery.html) · [ServiceNow: Exploring Problem Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/it-service-management/problem-management/exploring-problem-management.html)

question: The Problem table is extended from which table?
explanation:
In ServiceNow, the Problem [problem] table extends the Task [task] table and inherits its fields, rules, and policies.

**Learn more:** [Components installed with Problem Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/xanadu-it-service-management/page/product/problem-management/reference/installed-with-pm.html)

question: After a Catalog Item is requested, which mechanism determines the approvals and tasks that the application triggers?
explanation:
A ServiceNow catalog-item flow automates request fulfillment by defining approval steps and creating the required catalog tasks.

**Learn more:** [Now Platform Tokyo Release Fact Sheet](https://downloads.docs.servicenow.com/enus/tokyo/upgrade/tokyo-fact-sheet.pdf)

question:
A CAB manager is seeking a way to make CAB meetings more organized and efficient. They want to be able to:

- Define CAB meeting agendas
- View change calendars
- Review, approve, or reject changes directly from the change application

Which feature would you recommend?
explanation:
CAB Workbench centralizes CAB meeting management: it supports defining meeting agendas, viewing planned changes in a change calendar, and approving or rejecting change requests based on CAB decisions.

**Learn more:** [Change Advisory Board (CAB) workbench](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/cab-workbench.html)

question: Which record type should be used for a **View Company Policies** link that redirects to a Knowledge Article?
explanation:
A ServiceNow Content Item provides informational content rather than a requestable good or service. It supports the **KB Article** content type, which links users to the selected Knowledge Article.

**Learn more:** [Define a content item](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_AddingContentItemServiceCatalog.html)

question: When the ITSM Roles plugin is activated, which additional granular roles are created for the Incident application? (select 2)
explanation:
The ITSM Roles—Incident Management plugin adds `sn_incident_read` for read access to Incident Management records and `sn_incident_write` for write access; the write role includes the read role. ServiceNow documents these as the two granular Incident Management roles.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Components installed with ITSM Roles — Incident Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/inci-roles-instld-itsm-roles.html)

question: Before Quebec, when you select **Change > Create New**, which page is shown?
explanation:
Before the Quebec release, creating a change from the Change module opened the legacy Change Interceptor. Quebec introduced the new Change Landing Page for change models and preapproved changes, while preserving the interceptor for upgrade customers.

**Learn more:** [Breaking the Change Barrier](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-blog/breaking-the-change-barrier/ba-p/2294272)

question:
A tester intends to submit a bug report because they cannot see the **Communicate Fix** link under **Related Links** on the Problem form.

What do you recommend they verify before submitting the bug report? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Tester is impersonating a user with communications.manager role

options.label: B
options.text: Tester is impersonating the assignee, which has the problem_coordinator role

options.label: C
options.text: Tester is impersonating a user with problem_coordinator role

options.label: D
options.text: The Fix notes field is filled in and saved

explanation:
The **Communicate Fix** related-link action requires a role that includes `problem_coordinator`, and the Problem record must have content entered in **Fix notes** and be saved before the action can be used. Being the assignee is not required, and `communications.manager` is not listed as an authorized role for this action.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Communicate a fix](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-a-fix.html)

question: How can a customer configure additional notifications when the SLA Percentage Timer reaches 85%?

options.label: A
options.text: Use a newly created business rule to create an event

options.label: B
options.text: Use Flow Designer to add new action to the SLA notification and escalation flow

options.label: C
options.text: Use the SLA Timer Configuration to add new notification

options.label: D
options.text: Use the SLA Definitions to add a new SLA workflow

explanation:
The SLA Notification and Escalation flow is responsible for creating SLA notification events. Flow Designer supports SLA Percentage Timer actions at specified percentage values and allows notification actions or logic to run when the timer completes; therefore, an additional 85% notification is added to that flow.

**Learn more:** [SLA Percentage Timer action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/sla-percentage-timer-action.html) · [Flows for SLA](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-level-management/flows-for-sla.html)

question: What would you use to define a shared grouping of configuration items, such as all web servers in Miami?
explanation: A Dynamic CI group groups configuration items dynamically according to defined conditions, such as a web-server class and a Miami location. This supports a common, criteria-based grouping without manually maintaining membership.

question:
A customer wants a catalog that includes two items:

1. A request with 1 approval and 2 fulfillment tasks
2. A link to a knowledge article

Which item type would you use to meet the requirement for the Construction request?
explanation: A Catalog Item represents a request for a product or service and supports approval workflows and fulfillment tasks. It is therefore appropriate for a request requiring one approval and two fulfillment tasks.

question: Which catalog client script method modifies the choice-list options available to an end user on a catalog item?
explanation: An `onLoad` catalog client script runs when the catalog item form opens and can use client-side GlideForm methods, such as `g_form.addOption()` and `g_form.removeOption()`, to change the choices available to the user.

question:
Your customer reports that Service Desk users are repeatedly assigning Incidents to the Network CAB rather than Network Support. You have confirmed that:

- The Network Support group record has these Group types: Incident and Change.
- The Network CAB group record has this Group type: Change.

What could you do for the Assignment Group field on the incident form to resolve this issue?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a UI action to hide the Network CAB group from the list

options.label: B
options.text: Add a UI action to provide an error message if the Network CAB group is selected

options.label: C
options.text: Add Dictionary Override to specify the Incident group Reference Qualifier

options.label: D
options.text: Modify the choice list to include only the appropriate group types

explanation:
A dictionary override on the Incident table can apply an Incident-specific reference qualifier to the inherited Assignment Group reference field. Reference qualifiers filter the records available in a reference field, and dictionary overrides allow that qualifier to differ for an extended table. Filtering for groups with the Incident type keeps Network Support available and removes the Change-only Network CAB group from Incident assignment.

**Learn more:** [Configure assignment group types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/c_ConfigGroupTypesForAssignGroups.html) · [Dictionary overrides](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DictionaryOverrides.html)

question: Which type of service is published to service owners and is generally consumed only internally?
explanation:
A technical service is published to service owners and typically underpins business or application services, so it is generally consumed internally rather than being business-user-facing. ServiceNow now refers to this category as a technology management service (formerly Technical service) in its Service Delivery domain.

**Learn more:** [Service Delivery domain in the CSDM model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/csdm-implementation/concept/manage-tech-servs-domain.html) · [What are services and service offerings?](https://www.servicenow.com/content/dam/servicenow-assets/public/en-us/doc-type/success/quick-answer/services-service-offerings.pdf)

question:
A problem investigation was previously closed because the risk was accepted in favor of using the workaround rather than applying the fix. After a couple of weeks, the issue begins occurring more often, so management wants to revisit the root cause analysis.

What is the next step for this problem?

options.label: A
options.text: If 7 days has passed, since the Problem was closed, it cannot be re-opened

options.label: B
options.text: Problem Manager clicks Re-Analyze on the Problem record

options.label: C
options.text: Problem Assignee clicks Re-Open on the Problem record

options.label: D
options.text: Administrator clicks Re-Open on the Problem Record

explanation:
A risk-accepted problem that resurfaces should be reanalyzed. Selecting **Re-analyze** reopens the closed problem and moves it to the **Root Cause Analysis** state. The default role permitted to reanalyze a risk-accepted closed problem is the Problem Manager.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Investigate root cause of a problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/investigate-root-cause.html) · [ServiceNow: Problem management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-mgmt-properties.html)

question: Which role provides access to the CI Class Manager?
explanation:
The `ecmdb_admin` role is the CMDB administration role and grants the permissions needed to administer CMDB classes through CI Class Manager. ServiceNow’s current role model describes the successor `sn_cmdb_admin` role as providing full CMDB access, including CI Class Manager policy configuration; among the listed roles, `ecmdb_admin` is the applicable CMDB administrator role.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow system roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/base-system-roles.html?contentId=w6cANEQrbOf0hJZugq2tog)

question:
A customer has developed a mature knowledge base, including articles aimed at technical internal audiences and other articles written with simple instructions for end users.

From the Incident form, agents want to identify which articles are visible to callers. Which feature would satisfy this requirement?
explanation:
ServiceNow Contextual Search can be configured to search as a different user, such as the Incident record’s Caller. Its Search as user results apply the caller’s access context, allowing agents to see the knowledge articles available to that caller rather than internal-only content.

**Learn more:** [Domain separation and Contextual Search](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/contextual-search/domain-separation-contextual-search.html)

question: From a data-model perspective, which table serves as the base class for the configuration management database?
explanation:
Base Configuration Item [cmdb] is the core CMDB class in the data model. Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] extends that class and provides the basic attributes for configuration items. [CMDB schema model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ConfigurationManagementDatabase.html)

**Learn more:** [CMDB schema model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ConfigurationManagementDatabase.html) · [Configuration Item cmdb_ci class](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-table-property-descriptions.html)

question: When creating multiple catalog items, which components should be assessed for consolidation and reuse? (select 2)
explanation: Catalog-item development can reuse common process logic through flows and subflows, and reuse common input fields through variable sets. Consolidating these components reduces duplicated configuration across catalog items.

question: When the Assignment group is blank on an incident record, what occurs when an agent who belongs to a single user group clicks the **Assign to me** UI action?

options.label: A
options.text: The agent is prompted to select the Assignment group

options.label: B
options.text: The Assignment group field is populated with agent’s user group

options.label: C
options.text: An error is displayed indicating the Assignment group field must be populated before executing the Assign to me UI action

options.label: D
options.text: The Assignment group field remains empty

explanation:
For an agent who belongs to exactly one user group, the Assign to me action can unambiguously determine the appropriate assignment group and populates the Assignment group field with that group.

**Learn more:** [Work on an incident record in Service Operations Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/work-on-incident-sow.html)

question: Which table does the Incident table extend?
explanation: The ServiceNow Incident table inherits from the base Task table, whose technical name is `task`. This provides common task fields and behavior for incident records.

question: What are the key relationships between Change and Problem records? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Changes which cause Incidents, should have an associated Problem

options.label: B
options.text: A Problem can be solved by a Change

options.label: C
options.text: A Change can cause a Problem

options.label: D
options.text: A Problem must be associated with a Change, before it can be closed

explanation:
A Change Request can implement the permanent resolution for a Problem, and a Change may introduce an underlying issue that requires Problem Management analysis. A Problem does not need an associated Change before it can be closed.

**Learn more:** [Investigate root cause of a problem](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/investigate-root-cause.html) · [Problem management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/problem-mgmt-properties.html)

question: A customer has a catalog item named Request VPN. They want to customize the cart layout only for the VPN item so that the Quantity field is hidden. How would you meet this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: On the Cart Layout, Columns tab, unselect Quantity column

options.label: B
options.text: On the Catalog Item, Columns tab, unselect Quantity column

options.label: C
options.text: On the Catalog Item, Advanced View, unselect Use cart layout, select No quantity

options.label: D
options.text: On the Catalog, Advanced View, unselect Use cart layout, select No quantity

options.label: E
options.text: On the Catalog Item, Cart Layout Related List, set the Quantity record to Inactive

explanation:
ServiceNow supports cart-layout overrides at the individual catalog-item level. Clearing **Use cart layout** on the Catalog Item exposes item-specific settings, and selecting **No quantity** suppresses the Quantity field for that item without changing the cart experience for other catalog items.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow documentation: Configure the cart layout](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_ConfigureCartLayout.html)

question: Which role can modify the cart layout?
explanation:
The `catalog_admin` role has permission to configure Service Catalog cart layouts, including adding or removing cart components, columns, and buttons.

**Learn more:** [Configure Service Catalog preview screens](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/q4dSP2Icgr1SFv5wanVXvQ/cD8xDs0vQ8CMnu1~0RnrqA)

question: Which optional Incident table extends the Task table?
explanation:
Incident Task [incident_task] extends the Task table, inheriting Task fields and functionality while representing work items associated with an incident. ServiceNow documentation identifies Incident Task as an example of a Task-table extension.

**Learn more:** [Create Task step](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-task-action-designer.html)

question:
Given the class structure below, which CI types are included in a report run against the `cmdb_ci_computer` table?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783956775821-cj966hoc.png)

options.label: A
options.text: Just CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer

options.label: B
options.text: CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer and all parent classes

options.label: C
options.text: CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer and all child classes

explanation:
In ServiceNow table inheritance, a parent table contains records for its child classes. Therefore, reporting on `cmdb_ci_computer` includes CIs stored directly in that class and CIs in all of its child classes, but not CIs that belong only to ancestor classes. [Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg)

question: When defining SLAs for the service catalog, at which level is the SLA typically defined?
explanation:
Service Catalog SLAs are typically defined on the Requested Item (`sc_req_item`) record because each ordered catalog item has its own fulfillment lifecycle and service commitment. A single Request can contain multiple Requested Items, while Catalog Tasks are the work steps used to fulfill an item.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog request screens](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RequestingAServiceCatalogItem.html) · [How to create SLA for catalog item?](https://www.servicenow.com/community/community-central-forum/how-to-create-sla-for-catalog-item/td-p/3546370)

question: When a user submits a service request through a catalog, which actions are triggered according to the flow definition? (select 3)
explanation:
A Service Catalog flow runs the actions configured for the requested catalog item. Flow Designer can automate fulfillment tasks, approval requests, and notifications; access controls and action specifications are not fulfillment actions generated by the request.

**Learn more:** [Create a flow with a Service Catalog trigger](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/task/create-sc-flow.html) · [Flow Designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/flow-designer.html?contentId=rZaEg_PjkgH~nzf8rXjB9g)

question: A customer wants to provide business users with secure access to view problem records and reports for the products they support. When the ITSM roles plugin is installed, which additional Problem role is installed to meet this requirement?
explanation:
The `sn_problem_read` role provides read access to the Problem Management application and related records, supporting users who need to view problem records and reports without write privileges.

**Learn more:** [Components installed with ITSM Roles — Problem Management](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/prob-roles-instld-itsm-roles.html)

question: Your client says they would like a way to designate VIP callers on an incident form. How would you do this?
explanation:
A field style can conditionally format the Incident Caller field when the referenced user record is marked as VIP, making VIP callers visually distinct to agents without changing the field definition or running an action. ServiceNow release documentation also describes VIP indicators as field decorators in newer workspace experiences, but the standard incident-form VIP configuration is the VIP Flag field style.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Incident record page enhancements](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/xanadu-release-notes/page/release-notes/summary/rn-summary-new-features.html)

question: When is a Post Implementation Review change task created for an unauthorized change?

options.label: A
options.text: When the change request moves to Close

options.label: B
options.text: When a change manager accepts the change

options.label: C
options.text: When the change request moves to a state of Review

options.label: D
options.text: When the change request moves to a state of Assess

explanation:
For an unauthorized change, approval moves the change request to the Review state, at which point ServiceNow creates a Post Implementation Review change task for the Change Management group.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Unauthorized change request](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/unauthorized-change-request.html?contentId=UI1o4TBX_j9qJsWaVBI0Lw)

question: What is normally done to document the quickest known resolution when a Root Cause and a Workaround have been identified for a problem?
explanation:
A known error records a problem after its root cause and/or workaround has been documented, enabling support teams to use the established workaround as the fastest known means of resolving related incidents. ITIL problem management includes managing workarounds and known errors.

**Learn more:** [ITIL 4 Practitioner: Problem Management](https://www.peoplecert.org/browse-certifications/it-governance-and-service-management/ITIL-1/itil4-practices-problem-management-3688)

question: When using the **Knowledge - Instant Retire** workflow, how does the **Valid to** date take effect on a Knowledge article?

options.label: A
options.text: On Valid to date, article is automatically retired

options.label: B
options.text: On Valid to date, retire notification is sent to the Knowledge article author

options.label: C
options.text: On Valid to date, retire notification is sent to the Knowledge base owner

options.label: D
options.text: On Valid to date, the article is archived

explanation:
The **Valid to** field is the article’s expiration date. **Knowledge - Instant Retire** retires articles in the knowledge base without requiring approval; therefore, when that date is reached, the article is automatically retired.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a knowledge base](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/knowledge-management/create-a-knowledgebase.html)

question: Where can a change manager configure the interval frequency for detecting unauthorized changes?
explanation: The Unauthorized Change Properties module contains the feature-level configuration settings for unauthorized change detection, including the interval frequency used to run the detection process.

question: Which of the following is an appropriate use case for an Order Guide?

options.label: E
options.text: Order a case of Laundry Soap

explanation:
An Order Guide groups multiple related catalog items into one request and can use entered information and rules to determine which items are included. A custom automobile commonly requires coordinated, configuration-dependent components and options, making it a suitable Order Guide use case.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Order guides](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_ServiceCatalogOrderGuides.html)

question: In Change Management, what enables customers to define condition-based flows for a fit-for-purpose model?
explanation:
State Transition Models provide the configurable states, allowed transitions, and transition conditions for Change Models. They enable a fit-for-purpose change process to follow different paths when the configured conditions are met.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow plugin list: State Transition Models and Change Models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/platform-administration/list-of-plugins.html) · [Manage configurations in Service Operations Workspace for ITSM](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/manage-admin-console-sow-itsm.html?contentId=nltLTC4pVPk4kOBp3fOxug)

question:
In a conference-room reservation request form, the requester must identify the company location from the location table.

Which variable type is used to accomplish this?
explanation: A Reference variable points to a specified table and allows the requester to select a record from that table, such as a company location.

question: Which table contains incident categories and subcategories?
explanation: ServiceNow stores the available values for incident category and subcategory choice fields in the Choice table (`sys_choice`).

question: A customer wants incidents to close automatically 7 days after they are resolved. How can you meet this requirement? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to trigger from the Resolved date instead of the Updated date

options.label: B
options.text: Update the incident_close UI action script

options.label: C
options.text: From the Incident Properties application, set Enable auto closure of incidents based on Resolution date to Yes

options.label: D
options.text: Modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to expire after 7 days

explanation:
Incident auto-closure must be calculated from the resolution timestamp, not the record's last-updated timestamp. Configure the incident lifecycle to use the Resolved date and enable the Incident Properties setting for auto-closure based on the Resolution date. ServiceNow documents that this property switches auto-closure from the last updated date to the resolution date; the auto-close duration is configured separately in Incident Properties.

**Learn more:** [Configure incidents to close automatically](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/configure-incident-auto-close.html) · [Incident Management properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/incident-management-properties.html)

question: What is the relationship between Releases and Changes?

options.label: A
options.text: Releases are comprised of one or more Changes

options.label: B
options.text: Changes are comprised of one or more Releases

options.label: C
options.text: Releases are implemented prior to Changes

options.label: D
options.text: Changes are implemented prior to Releases

explanation: A Release is a package of one or more Changes that are planned and deployed together.

question:
Your customer is a data center with a construction department that builds out spaces for new customers. Customer account representatives are responsible for starting the construction requests. The guidelines for completing the construction-request documentation are extensive.

Your customer wants the catalog to include these two items:

1. Construction request
2. Getting Started with Construction Requests

The Getting Started item must include a link to a Knowledge Article.

What type of item would you use to meet the requirement for the Getting Started item?
explanation:
A ServiceNow Content Item is intended to provide information rather than a good or service. Its content type can be set to **KB Article**, which displays a selected ServiceNow knowledge article when the catalog entry is opened.
