**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Define a content item](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_AddingContentItemServiceCatalog.html)

question: When configuring stages in Flow Designer, which options can be performed? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Stage labels and names can be changed

options.label: B
options.text: States for the requested item records can be renamed

options.label: C
options.text: Define a Service Level Agreement for a stage

explanation: Flow Designer stages can have their names and labels changed, and an estimated duration can be configured for each stage. Service level agreements and requested-item state names are managed separately from stage configuration.

question: During which part of the Request Management lifecycle does the user complete the form for the item they are requesting?
explanation: The Specification phase captures the requester’s required information for the selected item through its form. The completed request can be submitted afterward.

question: A manager needs to run a report on the Computer catalog items to compare how many requests include the add-on extra memory with how many require only the base memory. How would you fulfill this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Build report on SC Task table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory

options.label: B
options.text: Build report on Requested Item table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory

options.label: C
options.text: Build report on Task table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory

options.label: D
options.text: Build report on Request table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory

options.label: E
options.text: Build report on Catalog Item table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory

explanation:
Each catalog-item order is represented by a Requested Item record, and catalog variables can be used to group reports based on the Requested Items table. Grouping Requested Item records by the Computer > Extra memory variable produces the requested comparison without counting multiple fulfillment tasks for one item. [Use service catalog variables in a report](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/use-service-catalog-variables-in-report.html?contentId=AYLVEOCU9OZeRIlebSuPfA)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Use service catalog variables in a report](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/use-service-catalog-variables-in-report.html?contentId=AYLVEOCU9OZeRIlebSuPfA)

question: When developing a service catalog, grouping items into categories helps users browse and search the catalog. Which roles allow you to create and maintain categories? (select 3)
explanation:
The `catalog_admin` role manages Service Catalog catalogs, categories, and items. The `catalog_manager` and `catalog_editor` roles can edit and update the categories within catalog(s) to which they are assigned. `catalog_builder_editor` is for creating and maintaining catalog items in Catalog Builder, not catalog categories.

**Learn more:** [Service Catalog terms and roles](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/yokohama-servicenow-platform/page/product/service-catalog-management/reference/r_ServiceCatalogManagementTermsandRoles.html)

question: Which Business Rule initiates automatic group assignment for Incident, Problem, or Change requests?

options.label: A
options.text: Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO

explanation:
The ServiceNow business rule named **Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO** automatically populates the Assignment group from the applicable configuration item or service offering for incident, problem, and change requests. [ServiceNow documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/create-change-sow.html?contentId=p4pnL8ns1qG95ZReHPtNUg)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Create a change request in Service Operations Workspace](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/service-operations-workspace/create-change-sow.html?contentId=p4pnL8ns1qG95ZReHPtNUg)

question:
Your customer wants to use the Normal change model, but also wants to add another approval level for changes related to the Service, SAP Enterprise Services.

What should you do to meet this requirement?

options.label: A
options.text: Add a new Policy Input to the Normal Change Approval Policy

options.label: B
options.text: Add a new Decision to the Normal Change Approval Policy

options.label: C
options.text: Add a new Change Approval Policy

options.label: D
options.text: Add a new Decision to the Normal Change Workflow

explanation:
A change approval policy can contain multiple decisions, and each matching decision applies its associated approval definition. The Normal Change Approval Policy's existing `change_request` policy input provides access to the change request and its referenced records, so an added decision can match SAP Enterprise Services and generate the extra approval level.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Change approval policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/change-approval-policy.html) · [ServiceNow: Create policy inputs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/create-policy-input.html?contentId=NbPoKuizc5gIFhSZfv78mQ)

question: Which practices are recommended for guiding your customers’ use of Notifications? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Make sure Notification requirements and test plans are in the project scope from the start

options.label: B
options.text: Get input from Marketing department, regarding format of customer/caller facing notifications

options.label: C
options.text: Use templates to ensure consistency and ease of configuration

options.label: D
options.text: Use incident.itil.role template as the master template to build all other ITSM templates

options.label: E
options.text: When possible, maximize the quantity of email updates to customers

explanation:
Notification requirements and test plans should be included in project scope from the outset so that triggers, recipients, content, and delivery behavior are validated before release. Marketing input helps ensure customer- and caller-facing communications use appropriate format and messaging. Reusable email templates provide consistent content and make similar notifications more efficient to configure. Excessive email updates should be avoided because notifications should be targeted and can be consolidated with digests when updates are frequent.

**Learn more:** [Email templates](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_EmailTemplates.html) · [Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html)

question: Which tool enables process owners to use natural language to automate approvals, tasks, notifications, and other record operations with little to no code?
explanation:
ServiceNow Flow Designer provides a no-code/low-code process-automation environment in which process owners can use natural language to automate approvals, tasks, notifications, and record operations.

**Learn more:** [Flow Designer — ServiceNow Documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/flow-designer.html?contentId=rZaEg_PjkgH~nzf8rXjB9g)

question: Which objects on the Shopping Cart Widget can be shown or hidden by using **Maintain Cart Layouts** settings? *(select 2)*
explanation:
The Shopping Cart Widget’s cart-layout configuration includes controls for displayed columns and components. Quantity can be configured as a cart column, and Price can be configured for display; ServiceNow documentation specifically identifies price columns/components and cart-layout controls that affect quantity.

**Learn more:** [Configure the cart layout](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_ConfigureCartLayout.html)

question: Which of the following is configured in the Assess Dialog Form View for problem records?

options.label: A
options.text: The notifications that are sent to Problem Analysts when a problem record is moved from the New to Assess state.

options.label: B
options.text: The text displayed in the dialog box when a problem record moves from the New to Assess state.

options.label: C
options.text: The users that receive notifications when a problem record is moved from the New to Assess state.

options.label: D
options.text: The fields which are required to be populated for the record to automatically move from the New to Assess state.

explanation:
The Assess Dialog Form View contains the mandatory fields required for a problem record to move automatically from the New state to the Assess state. ServiceNow documents this view as the location for adding the mandatory fields needed for that transition.

**Learn more:** [Add a field in the assess mandatory field dialog](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/add-field-in-assess-dialog-form.html)

question: You created a new Change model and added a new Approval Policy for that model, but the newly defined approval is not triggering. What could be causing this issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The business rule "Apply approval policy" on the change_request table has not been updated to include the new Approval Policy.

options.label: B
options.text: The "Apply Change Approval Policy" action in the flow created for the new change model does not reference the new Approval Policy.

options.label: C
options.text: The workflow that triggers the Approval Policy for the new model has not been created using the workflow editor.

options.label: D
options.text: The system property "glide.ui.approval.policies" has not been updated to include the new Approval Policy.

explanation:
Change approval policies are applied by a Flow Designer flow. The flow must use the **Apply Change Approval Policy** action and reference the intended approval policy; otherwise, that policy is never evaluated for changes using the model.

**Learn more:** [Modern Change Management – Adoption Playbook & Maturity Journey](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-articles/modern-change-management-adoption-playbook-amp-maturity-journey/ta-p/3279260)

question: Which fields on a Change request are used for conflict detection? (select 3)
explanation: Change conflict detection identifies overlapping planned change windows for the same configuration item. It uses the Configuration item together with the Planned start date and Planned end date.

question: Which Service Portfolio Management phase contains a service when it is in an operational state?
explanation: The Service Catalog contains services that are live and operational (or otherwise available for deployment). The Service Pipeline contains proposed or developing services, while Retired contains services that have been withdrawn.

question: Which process defines and manages the lifecycle of all catalog items by producing and maintaining the services in the catalog, while ensuring that a central, accurate, and consistent data source is available?
explanation: Service catalog management maintains the service catalog as the central, accurate, and consistent source of information about services and service offerings, including the information needed to manage catalog items throughout their lifecycle.

question: Which of the following are defined for a given change model? (select 3)
explanation:
A change model is configured with a state model, its state transitions, and conditions that control those transitions. ServiceNow documentation describes configuring model states, adding transitions between them, and defining conditions for those transitions.

**Learn more:** [Configure change model states](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/change-management/configure-change-model-states.html) · [Create a Change model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/it-service-management/change-management/create-a-change-model.html)

question: How can a customer modify the default priority from 3 + Urgency 3 to Priority 4 Low?
explanation:
ServiceNow Priority Lookup Rules map Impact and Urgency combinations to a calculated priority. Updating the applicable lookup rule changes the resulting value to Priority 4 - Low.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Define priority lookup rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/incident-management/def-prio-lookup-rules.html)

question:
ServiceNow has a resource that contains information about all services. It supports the sale and delivery of services to employees and customers, including details about deliverables, options, prices, and delivery and performance targets.

What is this resource called?
explanation: The Service Catalog is the centralized collection of service offerings and their associated information, including available options, pricing, deliverables, and service-level delivery or performance commitments.

question:
You have just upgraded your instance and have not migrated to Multimodal Change.

With the default settings, which page is displayed when you click **Change > Create new**?
explanation:
For upgrade customers, the legacy Change Management behavior is preserved by default until Multimodal Change is enabled or configured. The legacy Change Interceptor is therefore displayed when creating a new change. ServiceNow describes the new Change Landing Page as part of Multimodal Change and notes that the legacy interceptor is preserved for upgrading customers.

**Learn more:** [Breaking the Change Barrier](https://www.servicenow.com/community/itsm-blog/breaking-the-change-barrier/ba-p/2294272)

question: Released in Quebec, which tool enables you to create templates for Catalog Items?
explanation:
Catalog Builder supports creating catalog item templates, which can preset values and restrictions for Catalog Items created from those templates.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Catalog Builder](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-builder.html)
